  1483	\begin{proof}
  1484	We show the first item of the lemma for the case when $M^{(\Point,W),u}_a$ acts on register $\alice$ and $\tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a$ acts on registers $\bob \bob' \bob''$ (the argument for when the $\alice$ and $\bob$ registers are interchanged proceeds analogously):
  1485		\begin{align*}
  1486			&\E_{u \in \F_q^m} \sum_a \bra{\hat{\psi}} M^{(\Point,W),u}_a \otimes \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
  1487			&= \E_{u \in \F_q^m} \sum_{g,a} \bra{\hat{\psi}} (M^{(\Point,W),u}_a)_{\alice} \otimes (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\bob \bob'} \otimes (\tau^W_{\coded(g) \cdot \ind_m(u) -a}(\ind_m(u)))_{\bob''} \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
  1488			&= \E_{u \in \F_q^m} \sum_{g} \bra{\hat{\psi}} (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{\coded(g) \cdot \ind_m(u)})_{\alice \bob''} \otimes (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\bob \bob'} \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
  1489			&= \E_{u \in \F_q^m} \sum_{g} \bra{\hat{\psi}} (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{g(u)})_{\alice \bob''} \otimes (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\bob \bob'} \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
  1490			&\geq 1 - \delta_S\;.
  1491		\end{align*}
  1492		The second line follows from expanding the definition of $\tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a$ using~\eqref{eq:tilde_M}, the third line follows from the definition of $\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a$ given in Section~\ref{sec:expanding}, the fourth line follows from the fact that $\coded(g) \cdot \ind_m(u) = g(u)$, and the fifth line follows from \Cref{lem:qld-4-7}. This implies the first item of the Lemma.
  1493	
  1494	
  1495	To show the second item we first argue that, on average over $\tilde{u}$, 
  1496		\begin{equation}
  1497			\label{eq:qld-pulling-cons}
  1498			\Big ( \tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a \Big)_{\alice \alice' \alice''} \approx_{\delta_S} \Big ( \tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a \Big)_{\bob \bob' \bob''}.
  1499		\end{equation}
  1500		This follows because on average over $u \in \F_q^m$ and $\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits$ we have
  1501		\begin{align}
  1502			&\Big ( \tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a \Big)_{\alice \alice' \alice''} \label{eq:qld-pulling-0} \\

  1504			=_{\phantom{\delta_S}}& \sum_g \Big ( (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^W_{(\coded(g) \cdot \tilde{u}) - a}(\tilde{u}))_{\alice''} \Big) \cdot \Big(\sum_{r,s: r + s = g(u)} (M^{(\Point,W),u}_r)_{\bob} \otimes (\tau_s^W(\ind_m(u)))_{\alice''} \Big) \label{eq:qld-pulling-2} \\
  1505			=_{\phantom{\delta_S}}& \sum_{\substack{g,h: \\ (\coded(g)-h)\cdot \tilde{u} = a}}  (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \otimes (M^{(\Point,W),u}_{(g-g_h)(u)})_{\bob}~. \label{eq:qld-pulling-2b}

Thus for all $g \in \ideg_{d,m}(\F_q)$ and $s \in \F_q$ we have
  1508		\[
  1509			\tau^W_{(\coded(g) \cdot \tilde{u}) - a}(\tilde{u}) \cdot \tau^W_s(\ind_m(u)) = \sum_{\substack{h: \\ (\coded(g) - h) \cdot \tilde{u} = a \\ g_h(u) = s}} \tau^W_h~.

  1523	\end{align}
  1524		Line~\eqref{eq:qld-pulling-5} follows from~\eqref{eq:qld-pulling-4} by expanding the definition of $\{ \hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a\}$. Next, we argue that, on average over $u \in \F_q^m$,
  1525	\begin{align}
  1526			\text{\eqref{eq:qld-pulling-5}} &\approx_{\delta_S} \sum_{\substack{g,h,h': \\ (\coded(g)-h)\cdot \tilde{u} = a}} \Big((\hat{S}^W_g)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau_h^W)_{\alice''} \Big) \otimes \Big( (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{(g-g_h+g_{h'})(u)})_{\bob \bob'} \otimes (\tau_{h'}^W)_{\bob''} \Big)~. \label{eq:qld-pulling-7}

  1528			We show this by bounding the magnitude of the difference. Using the fact that $\hat{S}^W_g$ and $\tau^W_h$ are projective, we have:

  1538			\begin{align}

  1544			Before we justify the sequence of steps to go from Line~\eqref{eq:qld-pulling-7} to Line~\eqref{eq:qld-pulling-12}, we first argue how this establishes Line~\eqref{eq:qld-pulling-cons}, and hence the second item of the Lemma statement.

    38	\section{Key theorem forms}
    39	
    40	Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, let $\rho$ be an arbitrary
    41	density operator on $H$, and let $u\mapsto O^u$ be binary observables on $H$,
    42	indexed by $\mathbb F_2^t$.  The cited theorem assumes the averaged
    43	correlation estimate
    44	\[
    45	  \mathop{\mathbb E}_{u,v}
    46	  \operatorname{Tr}\!\left(O^u O^v O^{u+v}\rho\right) \geq 1-\delta.
    47	\]
    48	It produces an auxiliary space $H'$, a unit vector $\mathrm{anc}\in H'$, and
    49	binary observables $L^u$ on $H\otimes H'$ satisfying, with
    50	$\rho'=\rho\otimes|\mathrm{anc}\rangle\langle\mathrm{anc}|$,
    51	\[
    52	  L^uL^v=L^{u+v}
    53	  \quad\text{for every }u,v.
    54	\]
    55	Moreover,
    56	\[
    57	  \mathop{\mathbb E}_{u}
    58	  \operatorname{Tr}\!\left((L^u-O^u\otimes I_{H'})^\dagger
    59	    (L^u-O^u\otimes I_{H'})\,\rho'\right)\leq\delta.
    60	\]
    61	In particular, $L^0=I$: exact linearity gives $(L^0)^2=L^0$, while an
    62	observable is invertible.
    63	
    64	The chapter needs a parameterized version.  For each pair $(x,z)$ it applies
    65	the theorem to $(r,s)\mapsto O^{x,z,r,s}$.  Since the provider theorem accepts
    66	the actual nonnegative defect on each fiber, no assumption that a fiber defect
    67	is at most one, and no good--bad fiber split, is needed.  One must still
    68	formulate the finite common-extension step that makes the auxiliary space
    69	uniform over $(x,z)$.
    70	
    71	\section{Comparison with the quoted statement}
    72	
    73	Lines~711--725 of
    74	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex} quote the
    75	linearity theorem.  The displayed hypothesis correctly averages over both
    76	group variables.  The displayed conclusion, however, says that the corrected
    77	observable is close for every $u$, whereas Theorem~10 of the cited work gives
    78	closeness only on average over $u$ \cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}.  The quotation
    79	also inserts $\delta\leq1$, which is absent from the provider theorem and would
    80	unnecessarily obstruct applying it with a fiber's actual defect.  The assertion
    81	at the identity follows from exact linearity as above.
    82	
    83	Lines~825--832 construct the family $O^{x,z,r,s}$ and establish approximate
    84	linearity only after averaging over $x,z,r,r',s,s'$.  They then apply the
    85	single-family theorem separately for every $(x,z)$ and state that sufficiently
    86	many zero ancillas avoid a further extension.  The remaining implicit step is
    87	to make the theorem's possibly fiber-dependent auxiliary spaces uniform.
    88	
    89	The finite setting admits a standard repair.  Apply the theorem on each fiber
    90	with its actual defect, choose one finite auxiliary space large enough for all
    91	returned spaces, and embed each returned space so that its unit vector maps to
    92	one fixed vector.  Extend the conjugated observables by the identity on the
    93	orthogonal complement.  The embeddings may depend on the fiber because the
    94	observables do.  Averaging then yields the conclusion used later in the
    95	chapter.  This is an open reduction, not a counterexample to the quoted theorem
    96	or to the source's eventual combined-measurement conclusion.

    38	\section{Key theorem forms}
    39	
    40	Let $H_X$ and $H_Z$ be the positive contractions of the extraction proof, and
    41	let $\vartheta$ be a unit vector such that
    42	\[
    43	  \langle\vartheta,H_W\vartheta\rangle\geq1-\delta/2
    44	  \qquad (W\in\{X,Z\}).
    45	\]
    46	Since $(I-H_W)^2\geq0$,
    47	\[
    48	  H_W^2\geq2H_W-I,
    49	  \qquad
    50	  \langle\vartheta,H_W^2\vartheta\rangle\geq1-\delta.
    51	\]
    52	Also $\lVert(I-H_W)\vartheta\rVert^2\leq\delta$, whence
    53	\[
    54	  \lVert H_X\vartheta-H_Z\vartheta\rVert^2\leq4\delta.
    55	\]
    56	Together with $H_XH_Z$ equal to the EPR projection, these estimates give the
    57	required overlap bound, with constants absorbed into the stated
    58	$O(\sqrt\delta)$ error.
    59	
    60	For the final transfer, let $\phi\colon\mathcal H\to\mathcal K$ be an isometry
    61	and set $Q=\phi\phi^\dagger$.  If $N_h$ is the unitary-conjugated extension of
    62	a measurement operator $M_h$, then the exact identity is
    63	\[
    64	  \phi M_h\phi^\dagger=N_hQ=QN_h,
    65	\]
    66	not merely $N_h$.  Thus comparison of $N_h$ with an ideal projector must be
    67	combined with control of $(I-Q)\Delta$ on the ideal comparison state
    68	$\Delta$.

    70	\section{Numerical defects in the source proof}
    71	
    72	Lines~1715--1742 of
    73	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}
    74	construct $H_X,H_Z$ and identify $H_XH_Z$ with the EPR projection.  The norm
    75	estimate at lines~1743--1750 gives
    76	$\lVert(I-H_W)\vartheta\rVert\leq\sqrt\delta$.  At lines~1753--1757 the
    77	source substitutes $\delta$ inside the reverse triangle inequality
    78	\cite[lines~1715--1783]{Ji2020MIPStar}.  That replacement is not valid for
    79	small $\delta$.  The desired lower bound on
    80	$\langle H_W^2\rangle$ follows directly from $H_W^2\geq2H_W-I$, as above.
    81	
    82	The triangle inequality yields
    83	\[
    84	  \lVert H_X\vartheta-H_Z\vartheta\rVert\leq2\sqrt\delta,
    85	\]
    86	so its square is at most $4\delta$.  Line~1761 instead bounds that square by
    87	$2\sqrt\delta$ without a stated restriction.  This inequality follows when
    88	$\delta\leq1/4$; for larger error the theorem is made trivial by enlarging the
    89	universal constant.  The same small-error split ensures that the projected
    90	vector defined at lines~1769--1773 is nonzero before it is normalized.  These
    91	are local numerical repairs and do not weaken the extraction conclusion.
    92	
    93	\section{The range-projection obligation}
    94	
    95	Lines~1827--1858 prove state-dependent closeness for the concrete operators
    96	obtained by conjugating the original measurement with the swap unitaries.
    97	Lines~1864--1875 then define isometries by adjoining EPR pairs and applying
    98	those unitaries, and immediately state the corresponding closeness for
    99	$\phi M_h\phi^\dagger$.  The omitted range projection makes this implication
   100	non-definitional \cite[lines~1827--1875]{Ji2020MIPStar}.
   101	
   102	Let $\Psi$ be the original state and suppose $\phi\Psi$ is close to the ideal
   103	state $\Delta$.  Since $Q\phi\Psi=\phi\Psi$ and $Q$ is a contraction, the
   104	triangle inequality bounds $(I-Q)\Delta$ by the state-extraction error.  Using
   105	$\phi M_h\phi^\dagger=N_hQ$, split
   106	\[
   107	  (N_hQ-T_h)\Delta
   108	  =(N_h-T_h)\Delta-N_h(I-Q)\Delta,
   109	\]
   110	where $T_h$ is the ideal Pauli projector.  Summing squared norms over $h$
   111	uses projectivity and orthogonality to keep the second term under control.
   112	The same argument is required for each player and each Pauli basis.
   113	
   114	This transfer is an open proof obligation for the next extraction stage.  It
   115	must be a theorem derived from the concrete swap unitaries, transformed-state
   116	estimate, and operator comparisons.  It must not be stored as a bridge field,
   117	residual assumption, or hypothesis of the source-labelled soundness theorem.

  1671	There exists a function $\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q) = O(\delta_S^{1/4} + md/q)$ (where $\delta_S$ is defined in \Cref{lem:qld-4-7}) and unitaries $V_\alice$ acting on registers $\alice \alice' \alice''$ and $V_\bob$ acting on $\bob \bob' \bob''$ such that 
  1672	\begin{enumerate}
  1673		\item There exists a state $\ket{\aux}$ on registers $\alice \alice' \bob \bob'$ such that
  1674		\[
  1675			\left \| V_\alice \otimes V_\bob \ket{\hat{\psi}}_{\alice \alice' \alice'' \bob \bob' \bob''} - \ket{\aux}_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}_{\alice'' \bob''} \right \|^2 \leq \delta_\qld.
  1676		\]
  1677		
  1678		\item For all $W \in \{X,Z\}, h \in \F_q^\nqubits$
  1679		\begin{align*}
  1680			V_\alice \, \Big(M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \Big)_{\alice} \, V_\alice^\dagger &\approx_{\delta_\qld} \Id_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \\
  1681			 V_\bob \, \Big(M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h  \Big)_{\bob}\, V_\bob^\dagger &\approx_{\delta_\qld} \Id_{\bob \bob'} \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''}
  1682		\end{align*}
  1683		where the $\approx$ statements hold with respect to the state $\ket{\aux}_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}_{\alice'' \bob''}$. 
  1684	\end{enumerate}
  1685	\end{lemma}
  1686	
  1687	\begin{proof}
  1688	
  1689	Define the linear map
  1690	\[
  1691		V_\alice = \sum_{g_X,g_Z} (\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)))_{\alice ''}\;,
  1692	\]
  1693	where the $\tau^X(\cdot),\tau^Z(\cdot)$ act on $(\C^q)^{\otimes \nqubits}$. (Also note that the argument of $\tau^X$ is $\coded(g_Z)$ and the argument of $\tau^Z$ is $\coded(g_X)$.) We verify the unitarity of $V_\alice$:
  1694	\begin{align*}
  1695		V_\alice V_\alice^\dagger &= \sum_{g_X,g_Z} (\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) )_{\alice ''} \\
  1696		&= \sum_{g_X,g_Z} (\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes \Id_{\alice ''} \\
  1697		&= \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''}
  1698	\end{align*}
  1699	where in the first line we used that the measurement $\{ \hat{S}_{g_\xpt,g_\zpt} \}$  is projective and in the second line we used that the $\tau^Z$ and $\tau^X$ observables are self-inverse. The unitary $V_\bob$ is defined analogously.
  1700	
  1701	Let $\{e_j\}_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}}$ denote the self-dual basis for $\F_q$ over $\F_2$ specified in \Cref{sec:subfields}, and let $\tilde{W}^j$ be the observables introduced in~\eqref{eq:def-tildewj}. Conjugating the observable $\tilde{W}^j$ acting on the registers $\alice \alice' \alice''$ by the unitary $V_\alice$ we get
  1702	\begin{align*}
  1703		&V_\alice \, \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \, V_\alice^\dagger \\
  1704	  =& \sum_{g_X, g_Z} (-1)^{\tr( e_j(\coded(g_W) \cdot \tilde{u}))} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes \Big ( \tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \\
  1705	  &\hspace{24em}\tau^Z(\coded(g_X))^\dagger \tau^X(\coded(g_Z))^\dagger \Big)_{\alice ''} \\
  1706		 =& \sum_{g_X, g_Z} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes \Big ( \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \Big)_{\alice ''} \\
  1707		 =& \Id_{\alice \alice'} \otimes \Big( \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \Big)_{\alice ''}\;,
  1708	\end{align*}
  1709	where in the third line we used the (anti-)commutation relation
  1710	\[
  1711		\tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) = (-1)^{\tr( e_j(\coded(g_W) \cdot \tilde{u}))} \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \;.
  1712	\]
  1713	An entirely analogous calculation shows that $V_\bob \, \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \, V_\bob^\dagger = \Id_{\bob \bob'} \otimes \Big( \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \Big)_{\bob ''}$.
  1714	
  1715	Next, from the self-consistency property of the observables $\tilde{W}^j$ specified in \Cref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis} we get that for $W \in \{X,Z\}$,
  1716	\[
  1717		\E_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}} \E_{\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits} \bra{\hat{\psi}} \left ( \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \otimes \Id - \Id \otimes \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \right)^\dagger \left ( \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \otimes \Id - \Id \otimes \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \right) \ket{\hat{\psi}} \leq \delta_S\;,
  1718	\]
  1719	which, since $\tilde{W}^j$ is Hermitian, is equivalent to
  1720	\begin{equation}
  1721	\label{eq:qld-unitary-1}
  1722	\E_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}} \E_{\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits} \bra{\hat{\psi}} \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \otimes \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \ket{\hat{\psi}} \geq 1 - \delta_S/2\;.
  1723	\end{equation}
  1724	Let $\ket{\vartheta} = V_\alice \otimes V_\bob \ket{\hat{\psi}}$, and for $W \in \{X,Z\}$ define the operator
  1725	\begin{align*}
  1726		H_W &= \E_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}} \E_{\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits} \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \otimes \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \\
  1727			&= \E_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}} \Big ( \E_{s \in \F_q} \tau^W(e_j s) \otimes \tau^W(e_j s) \Big)^{\otimes \nqubits} \\
  1728			&= \Big ( \E_{s \in \F_q} \tau^W(s) \otimes \tau^W(s) \Big)^{\otimes \nqubits}
  1729	\end{align*}
  1730	where in the second line we used that for all $\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits$, $\tau^W(\tilde{u}) = \bigotimes_{i = 1}^\nqubits \tau^W(\tilde{u}_i)$ with $\tau^W(\tilde{u}_i)$ being the generalized Pauli $W$ observable acting on the $i$-th qudit. In the third line, we used the fact that for every fixed $j$, we have $\E_{s \in \F_q} \tau^W(e_j s) \otimes \tau^W(e_j s) = \E_{s \in \F_q} \tau^W(s) \otimes \tau^W(s)$. \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-1} is then equivalent to 
  1731	\[
  1732		\bra{\vartheta} H_W \ket{\vartheta} \geq 1 - \delta_S/2\;,
  1733	\]
  1734	for $W \in \{X,Z\}$. 
  1735	
  1736	Observe that
  1737	\begin{align*}
  1738		\E_{s,s'} \tau^X(s) \tau^Z(s') \otimes \tau^X(s) \tau^Z(s') &= \E_{s,s'} \sum_{a,b \in \F_q} (-1)^{\tr(as')} \ketbra{a+s}{a} \otimes (-1)^{\tr(bs')} \ketbra{b+s}{b} \\
  1739		&= \E_{s} \sum_{a\in \F_q} \ketbra{a+s}{a} \otimes \ketbra{a+s}{a} \\
  1740		&= \proj{\EPR_q}
  1741	\end{align*}
  1742	where to go from the first to the second line we used \Cref{lem:cancellation}. This implies that $H_X H_Z = \Big ( \E_{s,s' \in \F_q} \tau^X(s)\tau^Z(s') \otimes \tau^X(s)\tau^Z(s') \Big)^{\otimes \nqubits} = \ketbra{\EPR_q}{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$.
  1743	By the triangle inequality, we have
  1744	\[
  1745		\left \| H_X \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \right\| \leq \left \| \ket{\vartheta} - H_X \ket{\vartheta} \right\| + \left \| \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \right\|\;.
  1746	\]
  1747	Note that for $W \in \{X,Z\}$,
  1748	\[
  1749		\left \| \ket{\vartheta} - H_W \ket{\vartheta} \right\|^2 = 1 - 2\bra{\vartheta} H_W \ket{\vartheta} + \bra{\vartheta} H_W^2 \ket{\vartheta} \leq 2 - 2\bra{\vartheta} H_W \ket{\vartheta} \leq \delta_S\;,
  1750	\]
  1751	where in the inequality we used that $H_W \leq \Id$. Furthermore,
  1752	\begin{align*}
  1753		\bra{\vartheta} H_W^2 \ket{\vartheta} &=\| H_W \ket{\vartheta} \|^2\\
  1754		 &= \| \ket{\vartheta} + (H_W - \Id) \ket{\vartheta} \|^2 \\
  1755		 &\geq (\|\ket{\vartheta}\| - \| (H_W - \Id) \ket{\vartheta} \|)^2 \\
  1756		 &\geq (1 - \delta_S)^2 \\
  1757		 &\geq 1 - 2\delta_S\;. 
  1758	\end{align*}
  1759	Therefore 
  1760	\begin{align*}
  1761	2\sqrt{\delta_S} &\geq \left \| H_X \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \right\|^2  \\
  1762	&= \bra{\vartheta} H_X^2 \ket{\vartheta} + \bra{\vartheta} H_Z^2 \ket{\vartheta} - 2\bra{\vartheta} H_X H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \\
  1763	&\geq 2 - 4\delta_S - 2\bra{\vartheta} H_X H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \;,
  1764	\end{align*}
  1765	which implies that 
  1766	\[
  1767		\bra{\vartheta} (\Id_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} \otimes (\proj{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits})_{\alice'' \bob''}) \ket{\vartheta} \geq 1 - 2\delta_S - \sqrt{\delta_S} \;.
  1768	\]
  1769	Define the unnormalized state $\ket{\aux_0}$ on the registers $\alice \alice' \bob \bob'$ as
  1770	\[
  1771		\ket{\aux_0}_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} = (\bra{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits})_{\alice'' \bob''} \cdot \ket{\vartheta}_{\alice \alice' \alice'' \bob \bob' \bob''}
  1772	\]
  1773	and define the normalized state $\ket{\aux} = \frac{1}{\| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|} \ket{\aux_0}$. 
  1774	The inner product between $\ket{\vartheta}$ and $\ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$ can thus be evaluated as
  1775	\begin{align*}
  1776		\bra{\vartheta} (\ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}) &= \frac{1}{\| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|} \cdot \bra{\vartheta} (\ket{\aux_0} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}) \\
  1777		&= \frac{1}{\| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|} \cdot \bra{\vartheta} (\Id_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} \otimes (\proj{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits})_{\alice'' \bob''}) \ket{\vartheta} \\
  1778		&= \frac{1}{\| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|} \cdot \| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|^2 \\
  1779		&= \| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \| \\
  1780		&\geq \sqrt{1 - 2\delta_S - \sqrt{\delta_S}} \\
  1781		&\geq 1 - O(\sqrt{\delta_S})\;.
  1782	\end{align*}
  1783	This implies $\| \ket{\vartheta} - \ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits} \|^2 \leq O(\sqrt{\delta_S})$, which establishes the first item of the lemma.
  1784	
  1785	We now establish the second item of the lemma. In what follows, all $\simeq$ and $\approx$ statements hold with respect to the state $\ket{\hat{\psi}}$. From \Cref{lem:qld-win-implications} we have the following implications: for all $W \in \{X,Z\}$ and on average over $u \in \F_q^m$,
  1786		\begin{align}
  1787		\label{eq:qld-unitary-2}
  1788		M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''} &\simeq_\eps \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''} \otimes M^{(\Point,W),u}_a\;, \\
  1789		\label{eq:qld-unitary-3}
  1790		\Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''} \otimes M^{(\Point,W),u}_a &\simeq_\eps  M^{(\Point,W),u}_a \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''}\;,
  1791		\end{align}
  1792		where $M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} = \sum_{h : g_h(u) = a} M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h$. 
  1793	From \Cref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis} we get that
  1794		\begin{equation}
  1795		\label{eq:qld-unitary-4}
  1796			M^{(\Point,W),u}_a \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''} \simeq_{\delta_S} \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''}  \otimes \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a\;.
  1797		\end{equation}
  1798	Using \Cref{fact:triangle-for-simeq} with Equations \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-2}, \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-3}, and \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-4}, we get 
  1799		\begin{equation}
  1800			\label{eq:qld-unitary-5}
  1801			M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''} \simeq_{\sqrt{\delta_S}} \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''}  \otimes \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a\;,
  1802		\end{equation}
  1803		where we used that $\delta_S \geq \eps$. 
  1804		
  1805		Next, we have for all $u \in \F_q^m$ 
  1806		\begin{align}
  1807			&V_\bob \, \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \, V_\bob^\dagger \notag \\
  1808			= &\sum_{g_X, g_Z} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\bob \bob'} \otimes \Big ( \tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^W_{g_W(u) - a}(\ind_m(u))    \tau^Z(\coded(g_X))^\dagger \tau^X(\coded(g_Z))^\dagger \Big)_{\bob ''} \notag \\
  1809			= &\sum_{g_X, g_Z} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\bob \bob'} \otimes \sum_{h : g_h(u) = g_W(u) - a} \Big ( \tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^W_h   \tau^Z(\coded(g_X))^\dagger \tau^X(\coded(g_Z))^\dagger \Big)_{\bob ''} \notag \\
  1810			= &\sum_{g_X, g_Z} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\bob \bob'} \otimes \sum_{h : g_h(u) = g_W(u) - a} \Big ( \tau^W_{h + \coded(g_W)}   \Big)_{\bob ''} \notag \\
  1811		= &\sum_{g_X, g_Z} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\bob \bob'} \otimes \sum_{h : g_h(u) = a} \Big ( \tau^W_{h}   \Big)_{\bob ''} \notag \\
  1812	= &\Id_{\bob \bob'} \otimes (\tau^W_{[g_h(u)=a]})_{\bob''}\;,		\label{eq:qld-unitary-6}
  1813		\end{align}
  1814		where in the second line we expanded out the definitions of $V_\bob$ and $\tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a$ (defined in \cref{eq:tilde_M}); in the third line we expanded out the definition of $\tau^W_{g_W(u) - a}(\ind_m(u))$ (defined in \cref{eq:def-tauwu}) and used the fact that for all $h \in \F_q^M$, the inner product $h \cdot \ind_m(u)$ is equal to $g_h(u)$; in the fourth line we used the identities
  1815		\[
  1816			\tau^X(s) \tau^Z_h \tau^X(s)^\dagger = \tau^Z_{h + s} \qquad \text{and} \qquad \tau^Z(s) \tau^X_h \tau^Z(s)^\dagger = \tau^X_{h + s}~;
  1817		\]

  1819		\begin{align*}
  1820			\sum_{h : g_h(u) = g_W(u) - a}  \tau^W_{h + \coded(g_W)} = \sum_{h: g_W(u) - g_h(u) = a} \tau^W_{h + \coded(g_W)} = \sum_{h: g_W(u) + g_h(u) = a} \tau^W_{h + \coded(g_W)} = \sum_{h': g_{h'}(u) = a} \tau^W_{h'}~.

  1828		\begin{align}
  1829			&\sum_h \bra{\Delta} \left ( V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger - (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''}  \right)^\dagger \left ( V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger - (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \right) \ket{\Delta} \notag \\

  1837		&\approx_{md/q}  \E_u \sum_{\substack{h, h' : \\ g_h(u) = g_{h'}(u)}} \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_{h'})_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta} \label{eq:qld-unitary-8} \\

  1842		\begin{align*}
  1843			& \E_u \sum_{\substack{h \neq h' : \\ g_h(u) = g_{h'}(u)}} \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_{h'})_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta}  \\

  1862	We now prove \Cref{thm:pauli-appendix}. 
  1863	\begin{proof}[Proof of \Cref{thm:pauli-appendix}]
  1864		Let $\strategy = (\psi,M)$ be a projective strategy for $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ that succeeds with probability at least $1 - \eps$, where $\ket{\psi}$ is a bipartite state on registers $\alice \bob$. As mentioned at the beginning of \Cref{sec:commutation}, we assume that the state $\ket{\psi}$ is padded with sufficiently many ancilla $\ket{0}$ qubits. Let $\phi_\alice$ be the following isometry mapping the register $\alice$ to the registers $\alice \alice' \alice''$ where $\alice'$ and $\alice''$ are isomorphic to $(\C^q)^{\otimes \nqubits}$:
  1865		\[
  1866			\phi_\alice: \ket{\theta}_\alice \mapsto V_\alice (\ket{\theta}_\alice \otimes (\ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits})_{\alice' \alice''})
  1867		\]
  1868		where $V_\alice$ is the unitary acting on $\alice \alice' \alice''$ from \Cref{lem:qld-unitary}. Define the isometry $\phi_\bob$ analogously. \Cref{lem:qld-unitary} then implies that there exists a state $\ket{\aux}$ on registers $\alice \alice' \bob \bob'$ such that
  1869		\[
  1870			\left \| \phi_\alice \otimes \phi_\bob \ket{\psi} - \ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits} \right \|^2 \leq \delta_\qld
  1871		\]
  1872		and for $W \in \{X,Z\}$,
  1873		\[
  1874			\phi_\alice \, (M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h)_\alice \, \phi_\alice^\dagger \approx_{\delta_\qld} (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \qquad \text{and} \qquad \phi_\bob \, (M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h)_\bob \, \phi_\bob^\dagger \approx_{\delta_\qld} (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''}
  1875		\]

   832	\subsection{Polynomials and the low-degree code}
   833	\label{sec:ld-encoding}
   834	
   835	In this section, we introduce some basic definitions about polynomials over finite fields. 
   836	An $m$-variate polynomial $f$ over $\F_q$ is a function of the form
   837	\[
   838		f(x_1,\ldots,x_m) = \sum_{\alpha \in \{0,1,\ldots,q-1\}^m} c_\alpha
   839	  x_1^{\alpha_1} \cdots x_m^{\alpha_m}
   840	\]
   841	where $\{c_\alpha\}$ is a collection of coefficients in $\F_q$.
   842	We say that $f$ has \emph{individual degree (at most) $d$} if $c_\alpha\neq 0$ only if
   843	$\alpha_i \leq d $ for all $1\leq i\leq m$, and that it has \emph{total degree
   844	  (at most) $d$} if $c_\alpha\neq 0$ only if $\sum_i \alpha_i \leq d$.
   845	(Affine) \emph{multilinear} polynomials are polynomials with individual degree
   846	$1$.
   847	
   848	Low-degree polynomials play an important role in this paper.
   849	For one, the classical and quantum low-degree tests of \Cref{sec:ldt} are
   850	nonlocal games that efficiently certify that the players' answers are consistent
   851	with low-degree polynomials.
   852	Low-degree polynomials are also crucial in the probabilistically checkable
   853	proofs (PCP) construction that are used in ``answer reduction'' transformation
   854	(\Cref{sec:ans}).
   855	
   856	We recall the Schwartz-Zippel lemma: 
   857	
   858	\begin{lemma}[Schwartz-Zippel lemma~\cite{Sch80,Zip79}]
   859	  \label{lem:schwartz-zippel}
   860	  Let $f, g: \F_q^m \to \F_q$ be two unequal polynomials with total degree at most $d$. Then
   861	  \begin{equation*}
   862	    \Pr_{x \sim \F_q^m}[f(x) = g(x)] \leq d/q\;.
   863	  \end{equation*}
   864	\end{lemma}
   865	
   866	
   867	\paragraph{The low-degree code.}
   868	The Schwartz-Zippel lemma implies that the set of low-degree polynomials form an
   869	error-correcting code with good distance, which we call the \emph{low-degree
   870	  code}.\footnote{It is also known as the \emph{generalized Reed-Muller code} in
   871	  the coding theory literature.}
   872	
   873	Fix an integer $m \in \N$ and let $M = 2^m$.
   874	For every $y \in \{0,1\}^m$ define the following $m$-variate multilinear
   875	polynomial over $\F_q$:
   876	\[
   877		\ind_{m,y}(x) = \prod_{i: y_i = 1} x_i \cdot \prod_{i: y_i = 0} (1 - x_i) \;.
   878	\]
   879	Here, we identify $\{0,1\}$ as a subset of $\F_q$.
   880	Notice that, when restricted to the subcube $\{0,1\}^m$, $\ind_{m, y}$ is zero
   881	everywhere except for when $x = y$.
   882	For $a\in \F_q^M$, label the coordinates of $a$ as $a_y$ for $y\in \{0,1\}^m$
   883	(identifying the latter set with $\{1,\ldots,M\}$ using, say, the lexicographic
   884	ordering on strings).
   885	For any such $a$ define the multilinear polynomial $g_a: \F_q^m \to \F_q$,
   886	called the \emph{low-degree encoding of $a$}, as follows:
   887	\begin{equation}
   888	\label{eq:ld-encoding}
   889		 g_a(x) = \sum_{y \in \{0,1\}^m} a_y \cdot \ind_{m,y}(x)\;.
   890	\end{equation}
   891	Note that for any $y \in \{0,1\}^m$, $g_a(y) = a_y$.
   892	Furthermore, the map $a\mapsto g_a$ is linear: for every $x \in \F_q^m$,
   893	\begin{equation}
   894	\label{eq:low-degree-encoding-definition}
   895		g_a(x) = a \cdot \ind_m(x)\;,
   896	\end{equation}
   897	where $\ind_m(x)$ is the vector $(\ind_{m,y}(x))_{y \in \{0,1\}^m}\in\F_q^M$.
   898	
   899	\begin{lemma}
   900	\label{lem:ld-encoding-complexity}
   901	Let $q$ be an admissible field size, and let $M = 2^m$ for some integer $m$.
   902	The complexity of computing the evaluation of the low-degree encoding $g_a(x)$,
   903	given $a \in \F_q^M$ and $x \in \F_q^m$ represented in binary, is $\poly(M,\log
   904	q)$.
   905	\end{lemma}
   906	\begin{proof}
   907		Computing $g_a(x)$ requires computing the sum of products $a_y \cdot
   908	  \ind_{m,y}(x)$ over all $y \in \{0,1\}^m$.
   909	  Via \Cref{lem:efficient_arithmetic}, evaluating $\ind_{m,y}(x)$ takes time
   910	  $\poly(m,\log q)$ because it requires performing $m$ multiplications of $\F_q$
   911	  elements, and therefore the product $a_y \cdot \ind_{m,y}(x)$ requires
   912	  $\poly(m,\log q)$ time.
   913	  Computing the sum over all $y \in \{0,1\}^m$ requires $M \cdot \poly(m,\log q)
   914	  = \poly(M,\log q)$ time, as claimed.
   915	\end{proof}
   916	
   917	Finally, for any $H \subseteq \F_q$ we define the \emph{decoding} map
   918	$\coded_H(\cdot)$ which takes as input a polynomial $g : \F_q^m \to \F_q$ and
   919	returns the following vector $a \in \F_q^M$: for all $y \in \{0,1\}^m$, if $g(y)
   920	\in H$, then set $a_y = g(y)$, and otherwise set $a_y = 0$.
   921	Note that for all $a \in H^M$ we have $\coded_H(g_a) = a$ where $g_a$ is the
   922	low-degree encoding of $a$.
   923	For notational brevity we often write $\coded(\cdot)$ to denote the boolean
   924	decoding map $\coded_{\{0,1\}}(\cdot)$.

    93	\section{The range-projection obligation}
    94	
    95	Lines~1827--1858 prove state-dependent closeness for the concrete operators
    96	obtained by conjugating the original measurement with the swap unitaries.
    97	Lines~1864--1875 then define isometries by adjoining EPR pairs and applying
    98	those unitaries, and immediately state the corresponding closeness for
    99	$\phi M_h\phi^\dagger$.  The omitted range projection makes this implication
   100	non-definitional \cite[lines~1827--1875]{Ji2020MIPStar}.
   101	
   102	Let $\Psi$ be the original state and suppose $\phi\Psi$ is close to the ideal
   103	state $\Delta$.  Since $Q\phi\Psi=\phi\Psi$ and $Q$ is a contraction, the
   104	triangle inequality bounds $(I-Q)\Delta$ by the state-extraction error.  Using
   105	$\phi M_h\phi^\dagger=N_hQ$, split
   106	\[
   107	  (N_hQ-T_h)\Delta
   108	  =(N_h-T_h)\Delta-N_h(I-Q)\Delta,
   109	\]
   110	where $T_h$ is the ideal Pauli projector.  Summing squared norms over $h$
   111	uses projectivity and orthogonality to keep the second term under control.
   112	The same argument is required for each player and each Pauli basis.

    40	Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, let $\rho$ be an arbitrary
    41	density operator on $H$, and let $u\mapsto O^u$ be binary observables on $H$,
    42	indexed by $\mathbb F_2^t$.  The cited theorem assumes the averaged
    43	correlation estimate
    44	\[
    45	  \mathop{\mathbb E}_{u,v}
    46	  \operatorname{Tr}\!\left(O^u O^v O^{u+v}\rho\right) \geq 1-\delta.
    47	\]
    48	It produces an auxiliary space $H'$, a unit vector $\mathrm{anc}\in H'$, and
    49	binary observables $L^u$ on $H\otimes H'$ satisfying, with
    50	$\rho'=\rho\otimes|\mathrm{anc}\rangle\langle\mathrm{anc}|$,
    51	\[
    52	  L^uL^v=L^{u+v}
    53	  \quad\text{for every }u,v.
    54	\]
    55	Moreover,
    56	\[
    57	  \mathop{\mathbb E}_{u}
    58	  \operatorname{Tr}\!\left((L^u-O^u\otimes I_{H'})^\dagger
    59	    (L^u-O^u\otimes I_{H'})\,\rho'\right)\leq\delta.
    60	\]
    61	In particular, $L^0=I$: exact linearity gives $(L^0)^2=L^0$, while an
    62	observable is invertible.

  1419	Recall the decoding map of the low-degree code defined in \Cref{sec:ld-encoding}. This map takes in a polynomial $g \in \ideg_{d,m}(\F_q)$ and returns a string $\coded(g) \in \F_q^{\nqubits}$ consisting of the evaluations of $g$ on the points in the hypercube $\{0,1\}^m$.
  1420	We now use this decoding map to construct a new set of measurement operators out of $\hat{S}$.
  1421	First, we introduce some notation. For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$ and all degree $d$ polynomials $g: \F_q^m \to \F_q$ define projectors
  1422	\[ \hat{S}^X_g = \sum_{g_\zpt} \hat{S}_{g,g_\zpt} \quad  \text{and}  \quad \hat{S}^Z_g = \sum_{g_\xpt} \hat{S}_{g_\xpt,g}\;,\]
  1423	where the measurement $\{\hat{S}_{g_\xpt,g_\zpt} \}$  is given by \Cref{lem:qld-4-7}.
  1424	
  1425	For all $W \in \{X, Z\}$, $\tilde{u} \in \F_q^{\nqubits}$, and $a \in \F_q$, define the projector
  1426	\begin{equation}\label{eq:def-tauwu}
  1427	 \tau^{W}_{a}(\tilde{u}) = \sum_{h \in \F_q^{\nqubits} \,:\, h \cdot \tilde{u} = a} \tau^W_{h}
  1428	\end{equation}
  1429	where recall that $\tau^W_h$ is the projector corresponding to measuring $(\C^q)^{\otimes \nqubits}$ in the $W$ basis and obtaining $h \in \F_q^\nqubits$ as the outcome. For all $\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits$ define the projective measurement $\{ \tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a \}_{a \in \F_q}$ by 
  1430		\begin{equation}
  1431		\label{eq:tilde_M}
  1432		\tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a =  \sum_{g} \hat{S}^W_g \otimes \tau_{(\coded(g) \cdot \tilde{u}) - a}^W(\tilde{u})\;.
  1433		\end{equation}
  1434		If $\hat{S}^W_g$ is viewed as an operator acting on registers $\alice \alice'$ (resp. $\bob \bob'$) then we view $\tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a$ as an operator acting on registers $\alice \alice' \alice''$ (resp. $\bob \bob' \bob''$). (When necessary we will indicate via subscripts which registers the operators are acting on.)
  1435	The $\tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a$ are projective because the $\hat{S}^W_g$ and $\tau^W$ operators are projective.
  1436	
  1437	
  1438		For all $j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}$ define the observable
  1439		\begin{equation}\label{eq:def-tildewj}
  1440			\tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) = \sum_a (-1)^{\tr(e_j a)} \, \tilde{M}_a^{W,\tilde{u}} \;,
  1441		\end{equation}
  1442		where $\{e_j\}_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}}$ denotes the self-dual basis for $\F_q$ over $\F_2$ specified in \Cref{sec:subfields}. Let $\tau^W$ be the generalized Pauli observable defined in Section~\ref{sec:generalized-pauli}. Observe that
  1443		\begin{align*}
  1444		\Big ( \sum_{g_\xpt,g_\zpt} (-1)^{\tr(e_j (\coded(g_W) \cdot \tilde{u}))} \hat{S}_{g_\xpt,g_\zpt} \Big ) \otimes \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u})
  1445		&= \sum_{g_\xpt,g_\zpt} \sum_h (-1)^{\tr(e_j (\coded(g_W) \cdot \tilde{u}))} (-1)^{\tr(e_j(\tilde{u} \cdot h))} \hat{S}_{g_\xpt,g_\zpt} \otimes \tau^W_h\\
  1446		&= \sum_{g_W} \sum_a  (-1)^{\tr(e_j (\tilde{u} \cdot\coded(g_W) + a))} \hat{S}_{g_W}^W \otimes \Big( \sum_{h:\, h\cdot \tilde{u} = a}\tau^W_h\Big)\\
  1447			&= \sum_{g_W} \sum_a  (-1)^{\tr(e_j (\tilde{u} \cdot\coded(g_W) + a))} \hat{S}_{g_W}^W \otimes \tau^W_a(\tilde{u})\\
  1448			&= 		\tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \;,
  1449		\end{align*}
  1450		where the first equality uses the definition of $\tau^W(e_j \tilde{u})$, the second uses the definition of $\hat{S}^W_{g_W}$ and regroups terms, the third uses the definition~\eqref{eq:def-tauwu} of $\tau^W_a(\tilde{u})$, and the last is by a change of variables. These equations in particular show that the observable $\tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u})$ is Hermitian and squares to the identity, because the measurement $\{ \hat{S}_{g_\xpt,g_\zpt} \}$ is projective. 
  1451		Furthermore, it can be verified by direct calculation that the observables $\tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u})$ satisfy the same relations as the generalized Pauli group. Specifically, for all $j,j' \in \{1,\ldots,t\}$, $\tilde{u}, \tilde{v} \in \F_q^\nqubits$,
  1452		\[
  1453			\tilde{X}^j(\tilde{u}) \tilde{Z}^{j'}(\tilde{v}) = \begin{cases}

  1455			(-1)^{\tr((e_j \tilde{u}) \cdot (e_j \tilde{v}))} \tilde{Z}^{j}(\tilde{v}) \tilde{X}^j(\tilde{u}) & \qquad j = j'
  1456			\end{cases}~.
  1457		\]

     4	/-! # Polynomial decoding for Pauli extraction
     5	
     6	This module provides the Chapter 16 decoder on the Chapter 15 bounded
     7	polynomial representative type.  The generic retained-value decoder and its
     8	specialization to polynomial representatives live in
     9	`Algebra/LowDegreeCodeTheorems`; this module states the corresponding maps on
    10	`Poly P` used in the extraction chapter.
    11	
    12	## References
    13	
    14	The decoder is `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
    15	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, with the extraction use
    16	at `blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:11-20` and paper
    17	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1419-1450`.
    18	The restricted decoder identity and its encoding hypothesis are documented in
    19	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex:87-123`.
    20	-/
    21	
    22	open scoped BigOperators
    23	
    24	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    25	
    26	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    27	
    28	/-! ## Representative evaluation and decoding -/
    29	
    30	/-- Evaluate the polynomial representative carried by `Poly P`.
    31	
    32	This is polynomial evaluation on the source's `\ideg_{d,m}(\F_q)` carrier.  It
    33	does not identify representatives that induce the same polynomial function. -/
    34	noncomputable def evalPoly {P : AdmissibleParams} (g : Poly P)
    35	    (x : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) : PauliScalar P :=
    36	  MvPolynomial.eval x g.1
    37	
    38	/-- Decode a bounded polynomial while retaining only values in `H`.
    39	
    40	This is the `H`-parameterized form of `def:decoding-map`; `decodeAt` remains
    41	the decoding map for arbitrary functions.  The Boolean cube is embedded in
    42	`PauliScalar P` by `cubeEmbed`. -/
    43	noncomputable def decodeOn {P : AdmissibleParams}
    44	    (H : Finset (PauliScalar P)) (g : Poly P) : PauliRegister P :=
    45	  decodeAt H (fun x => evalPoly g x)
    46	
    47	/-- Full-field specialization of `decodeOn` used in Chapter 16.
    48	
    49	The retained-value set is `Finset.univ`, so every field value is kept.  This
    50	choice is the correction recorded in
    51	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex:87-123`. -/
    52	noncomputable abbrev decodeOnUniv {P : AdmissibleParams} (g : Poly P) :
    53	    PauliRegister P :=
    54	  decodeOn (Finset.univ : Finset (PauliScalar P)) g
    55	
    56	/-- The full-field decoder `\operatorname{Dec}_{\F_q}` on `Poly P`.
    57	
    58	The map `decodeFqRep` has the same definition on arbitrary polynomial
    59	representatives; `decodeFq` restricts its domain to the bounded-degree class
    60	`Poly P`. -/
    61	noncomputable abbrev decodeFq {P : AdmissibleParams} (g : Poly P) :
    62	    PauliRegister P :=
    63	  decodeOnUniv g
    64	
    65	/-! ## The encoding image -/
    66	
    67	/-- Membership of a multilinear encoding in the bounded representative class.
    68	
    69	The proof that the multilinear encoding has individual degree at most one,
    70	and hence at most `P.d` using `P.hd`, is a named proof obligation.  It is the
    71	degree side-condition implicit in the source's `g_h` construction, not an
    72	extra hypothesis of the decoding identity.  See
    73	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:381-401` and paper
    74	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    75	
    76	**Proof obligation:** issue #47 tracks the individual-degree calculation. -/
    77	theorem lowDegreeEncoding_mem_poly {P : AdmissibleParams}
    78	    (h : PauliRegister P) :
    79	    lowDegreeEncoding h ∈
    80	      MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc P.m (PauliScalar P) P.d := by
    81	  sorry
    82	
    83	/-- The multilinear encoding as a bounded polynomial representative.
    84	
    85	The individual-degree bound is supplied by `lowDegreeEncoding_mem_poly`. -/
    86	noncomputable def encodingPoly {P : AdmissibleParams} (h : PauliRegister P) :
    87	    Poly P :=
    88	  ⟨lowDegreeEncoding h, lowDegreeEncoding_mem_poly h⟩
    89	
    90	/-- A `Poly P` outcome is an encoding when its decoder reconstructs the same
    91	underlying polynomial representative.
    92	
    93	This is the explicit support restriction required by the corrected Chapter 16
    94	decoding argument.  It is the `Poly` view of `IsEncodingRep`; no unrestricted
    95	decoder/evaluation identity is asserted.  See
    96	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex:87-123`. -/
    97	def IsEncoding {P : AdmissibleParams} (g : Poly P) : Prop :=
    98	  lowDegreeEncoding (decodeFq g) = g.1

   101	
   102	/-- Linearity of the full-field decoder on bounded representatives.
   103

   105	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1442-1450` and blueprint
   106	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:11-20`.  It is a proof obligation; it does not
   107	assert evaluation equality for non-encoding representatives.  See
   108	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex:87-123`.
   109	
   110	**Proof obligation:** issue #47 tracks the regrouping calculation. -/
   111	theorem decodeFq_add {P : AdmissibleParams} (g h : Poly P) :
   112	    decodeFq (g + h) = decodeFq g + decodeFq h := by
   113	  sorry
   114	
   115	/-- Scalar linearity of the full-field decoder on bounded representatives.
   116	
   117	This companion has the same source and proof-gap status as `decodeFq_add` and

   119	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex:87-123`.
   120	
   121	**Proof obligation:** issue #47 tracks scalar linearity. -/
   122	theorem decodeFq_smul {P : AdmissibleParams} (c : PauliScalar P) (g : Poly P) :

   124	  sorry

   128	This is the identity `\operatorname{Dec}(g_h)=h` of
   129	`lem:qld-decoder-linearity`, blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:30-40`, for
   130	the full-field decoder specified at
   131	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1419-1420`.
   132	The degree proof is separated into `lowDegreeEncoding_mem_poly`; no additional

   134	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex:87-123`.
   135	
   136	**Proof obligation:** issue #47 tracks the decoder/encoding calculation. -/
   137	theorem decodeFq_lowDegreeEncoding {P : AdmissibleParams}
   138	    (h : PauliRegister P) :
   139	    decodeFq (encodingPoly h) = h := by
   140	  sorry
   141	
   142	/-- Decoder/evaluation agreement for an encoding representative only.
   143	
   144	The hypothesis `hg : IsEncoding g` is mandatory.  For a general bounded

   152	theorem decodeFq_dotProduct_indicatorVec {P : AdmissibleParams}
   153	    {g : Poly P} (hg : IsEncoding g) (x : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :

     3	/-! # Decoding maps for the low-degree code
     4	
     5	This file supplies `def:decoding-map` and the Boolean cube embedding from
     6	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper
     7	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`.  The specialization to
     8	polynomial representatives is `decodeFqRep`; its restriction to the bounded
     9	class `Poly` is defined in `Algebra/Decoding`.
    10	-/
    11	
    12	open scoped BigOperators
    13	
    14	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    15	
    16	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    17	
    18	/-- The formalization-only embedding of Boolean coordinates into a field used by
    19	`def:decoding-map`; blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper
    20	`04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
    21	def boolToScalar {K : Type*} [Field K] : Bool → K
    22	  | false => 0
    23	  | true => 1
    24	
    25	/-- The coordinatewise Boolean-cube embedding used by
    26	`def:decoding-map`; blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper
    27	`04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
    28	def cubeEmbed {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ} : Cube m → (Fin m → K) :=
    29	  fun y i => boolToScalar (y i)
    30	
    31	/-- On the Boolean cube, an indicator polynomial evaluates to the corresponding
    32	Kronecker delta.  This is the interpolation observation at paper lines 880-891. -/
    33	private theorem eval_indicatorPoly_cubeEmbed {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    34	    (y z : Cube m) :
    35	    MvPolynomial.eval (cubeEmbed (K := K) z) (indicatorPoly (K := K) y) =
    36	      if y = z then 1 else 0 := by
    37	  classical
    38	  rw [indicatorPoly, MvPolynomial.eval_prod]
    39	  simp only [apply_ite, MvPolynomial.eval_X, MvPolynomial.eval_sub, map_one]
    40	  have hfactor (i : Fin m) :
    41	      (if y i then cubeEmbed (K := K) z i else 1 - cubeEmbed (K := K) z i) =
    42	        if y i = z i then 1 else 0 := by
    43	    cases hy : y i <;> cases hz : z i <;> simp_all [cubeEmbed, boolToScalar]
    44	  simp_rw [hfactor]
    45	  rw [Fintype.prod_boole]
    46	  split_ifs <;> simp_all [funext_iff]
    47	
    48	/-- Evaluating a low-degree encoding at an embedded Boolean point recovers its
    49	coefficient at that point, as stated at paper line 891. -/
    50	private theorem lowDegreeEnc_cubeEmbed {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    51	    (a : Cube m → K) (z : Cube m) :
    52	    lowDegreeEnc a (cubeEmbed z) = a z := by
    53	  rw [lowDegreeEnc_eq_dotProduct]
    54	  simp [dotProduct, indicatorVec, eval_indicatorPoly_cubeEmbed]
    55	
    56	/-- The decoding map `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
    57	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
    58	noncomputable def decodeAt {K : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    59	    (H : Finset K) (g : (Fin m → K) → K) : Cube m → K :=
    60	  fun y => if g (cubeEmbed y) ∈ H then g (cubeEmbed y) else 0
    61	
    62	/-- Boolean specialization of `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
    63	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
    64	noncomputable abbrev decodeBool {K : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    65	    (g : (Fin m → K) → K) : Cube m → K :=
    66	  decodeAt ({0, 1} : Finset K) g
    67	
    68	/-- The full-field specialization of `decodeAt` for arbitrary polynomial
    69	representatives.  Its restriction to bounded representatives is defined in
    70	`Algebra/Decoding.lean`.
    71	Every value is retained because the filter is `H = Finset.univ`, so this is the
    72	cube-indexed evaluation of a polynomial representative.  The restricted
    73	decoder identity remains separate and is only available for encoding
    74	representatives; no unrestricted interpolation identity is asserted here.
    75	
    76	This is the `H = \F_q` reading of `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
    77	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, used by Chapter 16 at
    78	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:11-20`; paper origin
    79	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1419-1420` and
    80	the correction recorded in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex`. -/
    81	noncomputable def decodeFqRep {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    82	    (g : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) : Cube m → K :=
    83	  decodeAt (Finset.univ : Finset K) (fun x => MvPolynomial.eval x g)
    84	
    85	/-- A polynomial representative lies in the low-degree encoding image when it
    86	is exactly the multilinear representative reconstructed from its full-field
    87	decoder.  This predicate is used to state the support restriction required by
    88	the Chapter 16 decoding argument; it does not identify arbitrary polynomial
    89	functions with their representatives.
    90	
    91	See `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex:87-116`. -/
    92	def IsEncodingRep {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    93	    (g : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) : Prop :=
    94	  lowDegreeEncoding (decodeFqRep g) = g
    95	
    96	/-- The restricted decoding identity in `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
    97	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
    98	theorem decodeAt_lowDegreeEnc {K : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    99	    (H : Finset K) (a : Cube m → K) (ha : ∀ y, a y ∈ H) :
   100	    decodeAt H (lowDegreeEnc a) = a := by
   101	  funext y
   102	  simp [decodeAt, lowDegreeEnc_cubeEmbed, ha y]
   103	
   104	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

    33	/-! ## Heterogeneous extraction registers -/
    34	
    35	/-- One player's registers after adjoining the two generalized-Pauli
    36	registers: `AA'A''` or `BB'B''`. This identifies the register order and spaces for
    37	paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1429-1435,1687-1713` and
    38	blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:104-113,301-334`. -/
    39	abbrev ExtractionBlock (P : AdmissibleParams) (ι : Type*) :=
    40	  (ι × PauliRegister P) × PauliRegister P
    41	
    42	/-- The two heterogeneous extraction blocks in the order
    43	`AA'A'' | BB'B''`. This is the block presentation of the existing `SixReg`
    44	space used in `lem:qld-unitary`, blueprint
    45	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:348-375`, paper
    46	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/
    47	abbrev ExtractionRegisters (P : AdmissibleParams) (ιA ιB : Type*) :=
    48	  ExtractionBlock P ιA × ExtractionBlock P ιB
    49	
    50	/-- The auxiliary registers `AA'BB'` occurring before the extracted EPR
    51	factor in `lem:qld-unitary`, blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:348-375`,
    52	paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/
    53	abbrev ExtractionAuxRegisters (P : AdmissibleParams) (ιA ιB : Type*) :=
    54	  (ιA × PauliRegister P) × (ιB × PauliRegister P)
    55	
    56	/-- Reassociate the six-register order with the two extraction blocks.
    57	This equivalence identifies the register order in paper
    58	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1429-1435,1687-1713`. -/
    59	def sixRegExtractionEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) (ιA ιB : Type*) :
    60	    SixReg P ιA ιB ≃ ExtractionRegisters P ιA ιB where
    61	  toFun p := (((p.1.1, p.1.2.1), p.1.2.2),
    62	    ((p.2.1, p.2.2.1), p.2.2.2))
    63	  invFun p := ((p.1.1.1, (p.1.1.2, p.1.2)),
    64	    (p.2.1.1, (p.2.1.2, p.2.2)))
    65	  left_inv p := by cases p; rfl
    66	  right_inv p := by cases p; rfl
    67	
    68	/-- Shuffle `AA'BB' | A''B''` into the six-register order. This equivalence
    69	places the ideal state in the order used in `lem:qld-unitary`, blueprint
    70	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:348-375`, paper
    71	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/
    72	def extractionIdealShuffle (P : AdmissibleParams) (ιA ιB : Type*) :
    73	    (ExtractionAuxRegisters P ιA ιB ×
    74	      (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)) ≃ SixReg P ιA ιB where
    75	  toFun p := ((p.1.1.1, (p.1.1.2, p.2.1)),
    76	    (p.1.2.1, (p.1.2.2, p.2.2)))
    77	  invFun p := (((p.1.1, p.1.2.1), (p.2.1, p.2.2.1)),
    78	    (p.1.2.2, p.2.2.2))
    79	  left_inv p := by cases p; rfl
    80	  right_inv p := by cases p; rfl

    84	variable {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}

    86	/-- Place an operator on one complete extraction block, with the identity on
    87	the other player's block, as in the side-qualified operators of paper
    88	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1429-1435,1687-1713`. -/
    89	noncomputable def placeSide (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
    90	    (O : Op (ExtractionBlock P (S.LocalSpace side))) :
    91	    Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) := by
    92	  cases side with
    93	  | alice =>
    94	      exact reindexOp
    95	        (sixRegExtractionEquiv P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
    96	        (heteroKron O 1)
    97	  | bob =>
    98	      exact reindexOp
    99	        (sixRegExtractionEquiv P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
   100	        (heteroKron 1 O)
   101	
   102	/-- Lift an operator on a player's original strategy register to that player's
   103	full extraction block. This places the Pauli and point measurements appearing
   104	in `lem:qld-construct-the-paulis` and `lem:qld-unitary`, blueprint
   105	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:177-205,348-375`. -/
   106	noncomputable def onPlayer (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   107	    (O : Op (S.LocalSpace side)) :
   108	    Op (ExtractionBlock P (S.LocalSpace side)) :=
   109	  heteroKron (heteroKron O 1) 1
   110	
   111	/-- Place an operator on the original strategy register of the selected
   112	player. This is the player-side placement used in `lem:qld-unitary`,
   113	blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:348-375`. -/
   114	noncomputable def placePlayer (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   115	    (O : Op (S.LocalSpace side)) :
   116	    Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) := by
   117	  cases side with
   118	  | alice => exact S.place .AA' (heteroKron O 1)
   119	  | bob => exact S.place .BB' (heteroKron O 1)
   120	
   121	/-- Place an operator on the selected extracted register `A''` or `B''`.
   122	The unused strategy register in the crossed placement is assigned the
   123	identity. This is the placement of the ideal Pauli operators in
   124	`lem:qld-unitary`, blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:348-375`, paper
   125	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/
   126	noncomputable def placeExtractedRegister (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   127	    (side : PlayerSide) (O : Op (PauliRegister P)) :
   128	    Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) := by
   129	  cases side with
   130	  | alice =>
   131	      exact S.place .BA'' (heteroKron (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιB) O)
   132	  | bob =>
   133	      exact S.place .AB'' (heteroKron (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιA) O)
   134	
   135	/-- Place a pair of block operators simultaneously on `AA'A''` and
   136	`BB'B''`. This is the simultaneous placement used for the transformed state in
   137	`lem:qld-unitary`, blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:348-375`, paper
   138	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/
   139	noncomputable def placeBoth (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   140	    (VA : Op (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιA))
   141	    (VB : Op (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιB)) :
   142	    Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) :=
   143	  reindexOp (sixRegExtractionEquiv P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
   144	    (heteroKron VA VB)
   145	
   146	/-- Apply one operator to each heterogeneous extraction block. This is the
   147	witness-independent state transformation used for `V_A tensor V_B` in
   148	`lem:qld-unitary`, blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:348-375`, paper
   149	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/
   150	noncomputable def applyBoth (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   151	    (VA : Op (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιA))
   152	    (VB : Op (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιB))
   153	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ
   154	      (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)) :
   155	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) :=
   156	  applyOperatorToState (S.placeBoth VA VB) ψ
   157	
   158	/-- The state `aux tensor EPR_q^{tensor M}` in the six-register order.
   159	This is the ideal state in Item 1 of `lem:qld-unitary`, blueprint
   160	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:348-375`, paper
   161	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/
   162	noncomputable def idealExpState (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   163	    (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ
   164	      (ExtractionAuxRegisters P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)) :
   165	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) := by
   166	  classical
   167	  exact
   168	    reindexState (extractionIdealShuffle P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
   169	      (vecTensor aux (eprState (PauliRegister P)))
   170	
   171	end ProjectiveSetting

   173	/-! ## Coarse-grained Pauli projectors -/
   174	
   175	/-- Coarse-grain a finite operator family along a map of outcomes. This is the
   176	operator-valued sum corresponding to `Measurement.postprocess`, used by
   177	`def:tau-dot-product-projector`, blueprint
   178	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:85-93`. -/
   179	noncomputable def bracketOp {α β ι : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq β]
   180	    (N : α → Op ι) (f : α → β) (b : β) : Op ι :=
   181	  ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), N a
   182	
   183	/-- The effect of a postprocessed measurement is the corresponding
   184	coarse-grained operator sum. This equality is used by `def:bracket` and
   185	`def:tau-dot-product-projector`, blueprint
   186	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26` and `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:85-93`. -/
   187	theorem postprocess_effect_eq_bracketOp {α β ι : Type*}
   188	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]
   189	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (M : Measurement α ι) (f : α → β) (b : β) :
   190	    (M.postprocess f).effect b = bracketOp M.effect f b :=
   191	  rfl
   192	
   193	/-- The projector obtained by measuring in basis `W` and retaining outcomes
   194	whose dot product with `u` is `a`. This is Equation `eq:def-tauwu` in
   195	`def:tau-dot-product-projector`, blueprint
   196	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:85-93`, paper
   197	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1426-1429`. -/
   198	noncomputable def tauDotProj {P : AdmissibleParams} (W : PauliKind)
   199	    (u : PauliRegister P) (a : PauliScalar P) : Op (PauliRegister P) :=
   200	  bracketOp (pauliProj W) (fun h => dotProduct h u) a
   201	
   202	/-- Each dot-product coarse-graining is a projector, as asserted in
   203	`def:tau-dot-product-projector`, blueprint
   204	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:85-93`, paper
   205	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1426-1429`.
   206	
   207	**Proof obligation:** issue #47 tracks the orthogonal rank-one Pauli projector
   208	calculation. -/
   209	theorem tauDotProj_isProj {P : AdmissibleParams} (W : PauliKind)
   210	    (u : PauliRegister P) (a : PauliScalar P) :
   211	    IsProj (tauDotProj W u a) := by
   212	  sorry
   213	
   214	/-- For fixed `W` and `u`, the dot-product projectors sum to the identity.
   215	This is the completeness assertion of `def:tau-dot-product-projector`,
   216	blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:85-93`, paper
   217	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1426-1429`.
   218	
   219	**Proof obligation:** issue #47 tracks completeness of the generalized-Pauli
   220	projector family. -/
   221	theorem sum_tauDotProj_eq_one {P : AdmissibleParams} (W : PauliKind)
   222	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
   223	    ∑ a : PauliScalar P, tauDotProj W u a = 1 := by
   224	  sorry

   226	/-! ## Conjugation and extraction error -/
   227	
   228	/-- Conjugation of an operator by a square matrix, as used in the exact
   229	conjugation equations in `lem:v-swap-conjugation`, blueprint
   230	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:314-334`, paper
   231	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1687-1713`. -/
   232	noncomputable def conjBy {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
   233	    (V N : Op ι) : Op ι :=
   234	  V * N * Vᴴ
   235	
   236	/-- The common error scale for constructing the pulled-apart measurements from
   237	a global polynomial-pair witness. Here `deltaG` is its consistency error. The
   238	remaining terms record the point-measurement transfer
   239	and the Schwartz--Zippel loss; when `0 ≤ epsilon ≤ 1`, `sqrt epsilon` also
   240	dominates terms of order `epsilon`.
   241	
   242	This makes explicit the enlargement of the error called `deltaS` in
   243	`lem:qld-construct-the-paulis`, blueprint
   244	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:171-205`, paper
   245	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1458-1605`. -/
   246	noncomputable def deltaConstructPaulis (C epsilon deltaG : ℝ)
   247	    (m d q : ℕ) : ℝ :=
   248	  C * (deltaG + Real.sqrt epsilon +
   249	    ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) / (q : ℝ))
   250	
   251	/-- The explicit extraction scale
   252	`C * (deltaS^(1/4) + md/q)` from `lem:qld-unitary`, blueprint
   253	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:348-375`, paper
   254	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/
   255	noncomputable def deltaExtract (C deltaS : ℝ) (m d q : ℕ) : ℝ :=
   256	  C * (Real.rpow deltaS (1 / 4 : ℝ) + ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) / (q : ℝ))
   257

   226	/-! ## Conjugation and extraction error -/
   227	
   228	/-- Conjugation of an operator by a square matrix, as used in the exact
   229	conjugation equations in `lem:v-swap-conjugation`, blueprint
   230	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:314-334`, paper
   231	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1687-1713`. -/
   232	noncomputable def conjBy {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
   233	    (V N : Op ι) : Op ι :=
   234	  V * N * Vᴴ
   235	
   236	/-- The common error scale for constructing the pulled-apart measurements from
   237	a global polynomial-pair witness. Here `deltaG` is its consistency error. The
   238	remaining terms record the point-measurement transfer
   239	and the Schwartz--Zippel loss; when `0 ≤ epsilon ≤ 1`, `sqrt epsilon` also
   240	dominates terms of order `epsilon`.

   242	This makes explicit the enlargement of the error called `deltaS` in
   243	`lem:qld-construct-the-paulis`, blueprint
   244	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:171-205`, paper
   245	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1458-1605`. -/
   246	noncomputable def deltaConstructPaulis (C epsilon deltaG : ℝ)
   247	    (m d q : ℕ) : ℝ :=
   248	  C * (deltaG + Real.sqrt epsilon +
   249	    ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) / (q : ℝ))

   253	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:348-375`, paper
   254	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/
   255	noncomputable def deltaExtract (C deltaS : ℝ) (m d q : ℕ) : ℝ :=
   256	  C * (Real.rpow deltaS (1 / 4 : ℝ) + ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) / (q : ℝ))
   257

     4	/-!
     5	# Expanded registers and point measurements
     6	
     7	This module adjoins two EPR pairs to a heterogeneous Pauli-basis-test strategy,
     8	records the four register placements used in the analysis, and defines the
     9	expanded point observables and measurements.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	The constructions formalize `def:expanded-state`, `def:expanded-observables`,
    14	`def:expanded-point-measurement`, and `def:expanded-point-trace-projection` in
    15	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:760-874`. Their paper source is
    16	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:367-418`.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    20	
    21	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    22	
    23	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
    24	
    25	noncomputable section
    26	
    27	/-- The six registers `AA'A''BB'B''`, retaining distinct Alice and Bob local
    28	spaces. This is the register index type of `def:expanded-state`, paper
    29	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:367-372`, blueprint
    30	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:760-781`. -/
    31	abbrev SixReg (P : AdmissibleParams) (ιA ιB : Type*) :=
    32	  (ιA × (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)) ×
    33	    (ιB × (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P))
    34	
    35	/-- Equality of six-register indices is supplied by classical decidability for
    36	the register type. This is the index set of `def:expanded-state`; blueprint
    37	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:760-781`. -/
    38	noncomputable instance sixRegDecidableEq (P : AdmissibleParams)
    39	    (ιA ιB : Type*) : DecidableEq (SixReg P ιA ιB) :=
    40	  Classical.decEq _
    41	
    42	/-- Reassociate the tensor product of the strategy state and two EPR states
    43	directly into register order `AA'A''BB'B''` for
    44	`eq:def-psihat`, paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:367-372`. -/
    45	def sixRegShuffle (P : AdmissibleParams) (ιA ιB : Type*) :
    46	    (((ιA × ιB) × (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)) ×
    47	        (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)) ≃ SixReg P ιA ιB where
    48	  toFun p := ((p.1.1.1, (p.1.2.1, p.1.2.2)),
    49	    (p.1.1.2, (p.2.1, p.2.2)))
    50	  invFun p := (((p.1.1, p.2.1), (p.1.2.1, p.1.2.2)),
    51	    (p.2.2.1, p.2.2.2))
    52	  left_inv p := by cases p; rfl
    53	  right_inv p := by cases p; rfl
    54	
    55	/-- The four placements `AA'`, `BA''`, `BB'`, and `AB''` used explicitly in
    56	the chapter-14 consistency statements. Paper
    57	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:420-450`; blueprint
    58	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:876-922`. -/
    59	inductive Placement where
    60	  | AA'
    61	  | BA''
    62	  | BB'
    63	  | AB''
    64	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    65	
    66	/-- The strategy-player side supplying the local Hilbert space in each of the
    67	four register placements at paper
    68	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:420-450`. -/
    69	def Placement.side : Placement → PlayerSide
    70	  | .AA' => .alice
    71	  | .BA'' => .bob
    72	  | .BB' => .bob
    73	  | .AB'' => .alice
    74	
    75	namespace ProjectiveSetting
    76	
    77	variable {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
    78	
    79	/-- A strategy-local register paired with one generalized-Pauli register. This
    80	is the operator space in `def:expanded-observables`, paper
    81	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:374-382`. -/
    82	abbrev ExpandedLocalSpace (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide) :=
    83	  S.LocalSpace side × PauliRegister P
    84	
    85	/-- The strategy state tensored with EPR states on `A'A''` and `B'B''`, in the
    86	six-register order. This is `eq:def-psihat`, paper
    87	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:367-372`, blueprint
    88	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:760-781`. -/
    89	noncomputable def psiHat (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) :
    90	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) := by
    91	  classical
    92	  exact
    93	    reindexState (sixRegShuffle P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
    94	      (vecTensor
    95	        (vecTensor S.toStrategy.ψ (eprState (PauliRegister P)))
    96	        (eprState (PauliRegister P)))
    97	
    98	/-- Place an operator on one of `AA'`, `BA''`, `BB'`, or `AB''`, with the
    99	identity on all remaining registers. The input local space is determined by
   100	the placement, so no equality between the player spaces is assumed. Paper
   101	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:420-450`; blueprint
   102	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:876-922`. -/
   103	noncomputable def place (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p : Placement)
   104	    (O : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)) :
   105	    Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) :=
   106	  fun i j =>
   107	    match p with
   108	    | .AA' =>
   109	        O (i.1.1, i.1.2.1) (j.1.1, j.1.2.1) *
   110	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.2 j.1.2.2 *
   111	          (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιB) i.2.1 j.2.1 *
   112	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.1 j.2.2.1 *
   113	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.2 j.2.2.2
   114	    | .BA'' =>
   115	        (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιA) i.1.1 j.1.1 *
   116	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.1 j.1.2.1 *
   117	          O (i.2.1, i.1.2.2) (j.2.1, j.1.2.2) *
   118	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.1 j.2.2.1 *
   119	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.2 j.2.2.2
   120	    | .BB' =>
   121	        (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιA) i.1.1 j.1.1 *
   122	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.1 j.1.2.1 *
   123	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.2 j.1.2.2 *
   124	          O (i.2.1, i.2.2.1) (j.2.1, j.2.2.1) *
   125	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.2 j.2.2.2
   126	    | .AB'' =>
   127	        O (i.1.1, i.2.2.2) (j.1.1, j.2.2.2) *
   128	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.1 j.1.2.1 *
   129	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.2 j.1.2.2 *
   130	          (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιB) i.2.1 j.2.1 *
   131	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.1 j.2.2.1
   132	
   133	/-- The expanded observable
   134	`W^r(u) tensor tau^W(r * ind_m(u))` on a selected player side. This is
   135	Equation `eq:lc-23`, paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:374-382`,
   136	blueprint `ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:783-807`. -/
   137	noncomputable def expObs (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   138	    (W : PauliKind) (r : PauliScalar P) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
   139	    Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
   140	  heteroKron (S.pointObs side W r u)
   141	    (tauObservable W (fun h => r * indicatorVec u h))
   142	
   143	/-- The Fourier average defining the expanded point effect. This is the first
   144	display of `def:expanded-point-measurement`, paper
   145	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:384-418`, blueprint
   146	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:809-844`. -/
   147	noncomputable def expPointOp (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   148	    (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (a : PauliScalar P) :
   149	    Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
   150	  averageOperatorOverDistribution (uniformDistribution (PauliScalar P)) fun r =>
   151	    phaseSign (fixedBinTrace P.model (a * r)) • S.expObs side W r u
   152	
   153	/-- The Pauli-register projector onto labels whose low-degree encoding has
   154	value `a` at `u`. This is Equation `eq:qld-point-obs-def`, paper
   155	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:389-394`, blueprint
   156	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:809-844`. -/
   157	noncomputable def tauPointProj (W : PauliKind)
   158	    (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (a : PauliScalar P) : Op (PauliRegister P) :=
   159	  ∑ h ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun h : PauliRegister P =>
   160	      dotProduct h (indicatorVec u) = a),
   161	    pauliProj W h
   162	
   163	/-- Expanded point effects are positive semidefinite. This is the positivity
   164	obligation in `def:expanded-point-measurement`, paper
   165	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:384-418`. -/
   166	theorem expPointOp_nonneg (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   167	    (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (a : PauliScalar P) :
   168	    0 ≤ S.expPointOp side W u a := by
   169	  sorry
   170	
   171	/-- Expanded point effects sum to the identity. This is the completeness
   172	obligation in `def:expanded-point-measurement`, paper
   173	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:384-418`. -/
   174	theorem expPointOp_sum_eq_one (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   175	    (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
   176	    ∑ a, S.expPointOp side W u a = 1 := by
   177	  sorry
   178	
   179	/-- The complete expanded point measurement on the chosen player and Pauli
   180	register. Its effects are those of `def:expanded-point-measurement`, paper
   181	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:384-418`, blueprint
   182	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:809-844`. -/
   183	noncomputable def pointMeasExp (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   184	    (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
   185	    Measurement (PauliScalar P) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
   186	  Measurement.ofSumEqOne (S.expPointOp side W u)
   187	    (S.expPointOp_nonneg side W u) (S.expPointOp_sum_eq_one side W u)
   188	
   189	/-- The expanded point effect is the convolution of the strategy point
   190	measurement and the Pauli-register point projection. This is the final display
   191	of `def:expanded-point-measurement`, paper
   192	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:395-418`. -/
   193	theorem expPointOp_eq_convolution (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   194	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   195	    (a : PauliScalar P) :
   196	    S.expPointOp side W u a =
   197	      ∑ p ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun p : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P =>
   198	          p.1 + p.2 = a),
   199	        heteroKron ((S.pointMeas side W u).effect p.1)
   200	          (tauPointProj W u p.2) := by

   202

   204	convolution formula in `def:expanded-point-measurement`, paper
   205	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:395-418`. -/
   206	theorem pointMeasExp_isProjective (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   207	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
   208	    MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (S.pointMeasExp side W u) := by
   209	  sorry
   210	
   211	/-- Trace-coarse-graining of the expanded point measurement. This is Equation
   212	`eq:qld-def-mptur`, paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:411-418`,
   213	blueprint `ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:846-874`. -/
   214	noncomputable def expPointTrace (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   215	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   216	    (r : PauliScalar P) : Measurement (ZMod 2) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
   217	  (S.pointMeasExp side W u).postprocess fun a => fixedBinTrace P.model (a * r)
   218	
   219	/-- Fourier inversion writes a trace-coarse-grained point effect as one half
   220	of the identity plus its signed expanded observable. This is Equation
   221	`eq:lc-22`, paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:411-418`, blueprint
   222	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:846-874`. -/
   223	theorem expPointTrace_eq_half_add (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   224	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   225	    (r : PauliScalar P) (b : ZMod 2) :
   226	    (S.expPointTrace side W u r).effect b =
   227	      (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ •
   228	        (1 + phaseSign b • S.expObs side W r u) := by
   229	  sorry
   230	
   231	end ProjectiveSetting
   232	
   233	end

     7	
     8	This file fixes a projective, possibly heterogeneous strategy for the Pauli
     9	basis test and extracts the typed measurement families used in the analysis.
    10	Malformed answers are folded into a fixed valid answer, so the extracted
    11	families remain complete measurements. The winning hypothesis bounds their
    12	original wrong-form mass by the rejection probability. `Option` is used only
    13	for the completed line-evaluation classes.

    18	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:160-190`,
    19	corresponding to `def:strategy-observables` in
    20	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:480-503`. The typed question

    22	`def:pauli-win-predicate`, paper
    23	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1225`

    60	def LocalSpace (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) : PlayerSide → Type

    64	instance localSpaceFintype (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide) :

    72	/-- Select the strategy measurement before outcome postprocessing on one
    73	player side. This is the heterogeneous interpretation of the shared symbol `M` at
    74	paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:160-184`. -/

    76	    (question : PauliQuestion P) :

    82	/-- Embed a point into the full Pauli question space in basis `W`. This is the

    84	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:997-1008`, blueprint
    85	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:310-354`. -/
    86	def contentOfPoint (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
    87	    (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) : PauliSpace P :=
    88	  embedLd P W fun i =>
    89	    match i with
    90	    | .inl (.inl j) => u j
    91	    | .inl (.inr _) => 0
    92	    | .inr _ => 0
    93	
    94	/-- Embed a canonical line description into the full Pauli question space.
    95	Axis lines clear the direction block, whereas diagonal lines retain their

    97	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:997-1008`; blueprint
    98	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:310-354` and `rem:deg-line-representatives`. -/
    99	def contentOfLine (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   100	    (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams) : PauliSpace P :=
