   102	    match i with
   103	    | .inl (.inl j) => line.base j
   104	    | .inl (.inr _) => line.seed
   105	    | .inr j =>
   106	        match line with
   107	        | .axis _ _ _ => 0
   108	        | .diagonal _ _ direction _ _ => direction j
   109	
   110	/-- Fill the point, scalar, and phase blocks shared by Pair, Pair/W, and Magic
   111	Square questions. This is the type-4 content of
   112	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, paper
   113	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1030-1120`, blueprint
   114	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:310-354`. -/
   115	def contentOfTuple (P : AdmissibleParams)
   275	      match answer with
   276	      | .msTriple bits => .triple bits
   277	      | _ => .triple 0
   278	  | .var _ => fun answer =>
   279	      match answer with
   280	      | .bit bit => .bit bit
   281	      | _ => .bit 0
   282	
   283	/-- The complete typed point measurement on one player side. It is the
   284	corresponding strategy measurement postprocessed by `pointAnswerOrZero`; paper
   285	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:174-190`, blueprint
   286	`def:strategy-observables`. -/
   287	noncomputable def pointMeas (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   288	    (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
   289	    Measurement (PauliScalar P) (S.LocalSpace side) :=
   290	  (S.strategyMeasurement side (pointQuestion P W u)).postprocess pointAnswerOrZero
   291	
   292	/-- The complete typed line measurement on one player side, uniformly indexed
   293	by degree-`m*d` coefficient lists. Paper
   294	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:174-184`; blueprint
   295	`def:ideg-deg-polynomials` and `lem:qld-win-implications`. -/
   296	noncomputable def lineMeas (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   297	    (W : PauliKind) (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams) :
   298	    Measurement (DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d)) (S.LocalSpace side) :=
   299	  (S.strategyMeasurement side (lineQuestion P W line)).postprocess
   300	    (lineAnswerOrZero P line)
   301	
   302	/-- The completed evaluation classes of a typed line measurement. This is the
   303	only strategy-side family whose outcome uses `Option`; `none` is precisely the
   304	non-evaluating class of `def:ideg-deg-polynomials`, paper
   305	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:51-62`, blueprint
   306	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:51-118`. -/
   307	noncomputable def lineEvalMeas (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   308	    (W : PauliKind) (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams)
   309	    (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
   310	    Measurement (Option (PauliScalar P)) (S.LocalSpace side) :=
   311	  (S.lineMeas side W line).postprocess (evalOpt line u)
   312	
   313	/-- The complete typed Pair measurement on one player side. Paper
   314	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:210-249`; blueprint
   315	`lem:qld-win-implications`. -/
   316	noncomputable def pairMeas (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   317	    (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) :
   318	    Measurement (ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) (S.LocalSpace side) :=
   319	  (S.strategyMeasurement side (pairQuestion P uX uZ rX rZ)).postprocess pairAnswerOrZero
   320	
   321	/-- The complete typed Pair/W measurement on one player side. Paper
   322	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:210-263`; blueprint
   323	`lem:qld-win-implications`. -/
   324	noncomputable def pairWMeas (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   325	    (W : PauliKind) (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   326	    (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) : Measurement (ZMod 2) (S.LocalSpace side) :=
   327	  (S.strategyMeasurement side (pairWQuestion P W uX uZ rX rZ)).postprocess
   328	    pairWAnswerOrZero
   329	
   330	/-- The complete typed Pauli/W measurement on one player side. Paper
   331	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:205-209`; blueprint
   332	`lem:qld-win-implications`. -/
   333	noncomputable def pauliMeas (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   334	    (W : PauliKind) : Measurement (PauliRegister P) (S.LocalSpace side) :=
   335	  (S.strategyMeasurement side (pauliQuestion P W)).postprocess pauliAnswerOrZero
   336	
   337	/-- The complete typed Magic Square measurement on one player side. Its answer
   338	alphabet is exactly `MsAnswer`; these families therefore define a Magic Square
   339	strategy. Paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:213-258`;
   340	blueprint `lem:qld-win-implications`. -/
   341	noncomputable def msMeas (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   342	    (t : MsType) (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   343	    (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) : Measurement MsAnswer (S.LocalSpace side) :=
   344	  (S.strategyMeasurement side (msQuestion P t uX uZ rX rZ)).postprocess
   345	    (msAnswerOrZero t)
   346	
   347	/-- The sum of effects corresponding to answers that are invalid for a given
   348	question type. This mass is kept separate from the fixed valid outcome into

   350	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`, blueprint

   352	noncomputable def wrongFormEffect {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   353	    (t : PauliType) (M : Measurement (PauliAnswer P) ι) : Op ι :=
   354	  ∑ answer ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun answer => validPauliAnswer t answer = false),

     4	/-!
     5	# Polynomial combination and restricted line distributions
     6	
     7	This file contains the concrete definitions at the foundation of the
     8	Chapter 15 combining argument.  A pair of bounded individual-degree
     9	polynomials is embedded into the two coordinate blocks of an extended
    10	polynomial.  On lines, explicit affine reparameterizations are composed with
    11	coefficient-list polynomials.  The original-dimensional restricted line laws
    12	are formed before decoding, while their field seed is still present.
    13	
    14	## References
    15	
    16	The combining map is `def:combine-map` in
    17	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:445-480`, with paper origin
    18	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`.
    19	The restricted laws are `def:ith-restricted-line` in blueprint lines 578--592,
    20	with paper origin in the same source at lines 1038--1048.
    21	-/
    22	
    23	open scoped BigOperators
    24	
    25	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    26	
    27	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    28	open MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    29	
    30	noncomputable section
    31	
    32	/-- The bounded individual-degree polynomial outcome used by the global
    33	pair measurement.  This is the actual `polyFunc` subtype from
    34	`def:polyfunc`, not a coefficient-box replacement. -/
    35	noncomputable abbrev Poly (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
    36	  ↥(MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc P.m (PauliScalar P) P.d)
    37	
    38	/-- Pairs of bounded polynomial representatives returned by the global
    39	measurement in `lem:qld-4-7`. -/
    40	noncomputable abbrev PolyPair (P : AdmissibleParams) := Poly P × Poly P
    41	
    42	/-- Split the extended coordinate set into the `X` block, the `Z` block, and
    43	the two scalar coordinates.  This is formalization-only coordinate plumbing
    44	for `def:combine-map`, blueprint
    45	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:445-480`, paper
    46	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    47	def finCombineEquiv (m : ℕ) :
    48	    Fin (2 * m + 2) ≃ ((Fin m ⊕ Fin m) ⊕ Fin 2) :=
    49	  (finCongr (by omega)).trans
    50	    (finSumFinEquiv.symm.trans
    51	      (Equiv.sumCongr finSumFinEquiv.symm (Equiv.refl (Fin 2))))
    52	
    53	/-- Embed an `X`-block coordinate into the extended coordinate set. -/
    54	def embX (m : ℕ) : Fin m → Fin (2 * m + 2) :=
    55	  fun i => (finCombineEquiv m).symm (.inl (.inl i))
    56	
    57	/-- Embed a `Z`-block coordinate into the extended coordinate set. -/
    58	def embZ (m : ℕ) : Fin m → Fin (2 * m + 2) :=
    59	  fun i => (finCombineEquiv m).symm (.inl (.inr i))
    60	
    61	/-- The extended coordinate occupied by the scalar `alpha`. -/
    62	def alphaVar (m : ℕ) : Fin (2 * m + 2) :=
    63	  (finCombineEquiv m).symm (.inr 0)
    64	
    65	/-- The extended coordinate occupied by the scalar `beta`. -/
    66	def betaVar (m : ℕ) : Fin (2 * m + 2) :=
    67	  (finCombineEquiv m).symm (.inr 1)
    68	
    69	/-- Project an extended point onto its `X` coordinate block. -/
    70	def projX {K : Type*} {m : ℕ} (u : Fin (2 * m + 2) → K) : Fin m → K :=
    71	  fun i => u (embX m i)
    72	
    73	/-- Project an extended point onto its `Z` coordinate block. -/
    74	def projZ {K : Type*} {m : ℕ} (u : Fin (2 * m + 2) → K) : Fin m → K :=
    75	  fun i => u (embZ m i)
    76	
    77	/-- Combine two multivariate polynomials by the formula
    78	`alpha * f(x) + beta * g(z)` from `def:combine-map`.
    79	
    80	Blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:445-480`; paper

     5	/-!
     6	# Expanded point consistency and commutation
     7	
     8	This module records the quantitative conclusions for the expanded point
     9	measurements on each of the four register placements. No symmetry-transfer
    10	principle is assumed: the four placements occur explicitly in the statements.
    11	
    12	## References
    13	
    14	The declarations formalize `lem:qld-comm-cons` in
    15	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:932-1032`, whose paper source
    16	is `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:452-505`.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    20	
    21	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
    22	
    23	noncomputable section
    24	
    25	/-- The four directed cross-party placement pairs asserted by the source's
    26	“symmetric equivalents” clause. The relation lists the two orientations of
    27	each of the `AA'`--`BA''` and `BB'`--`AB''` pairs; paper
    28	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:420-450`, blueprint
    29	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:876-922`. -/
    30	def Placement.IsOpposite : Placement → Placement → Prop
    31	  | .AA', .BA'' => True
    32	  | .BA'', .AA' => True
    33	  | .BB', .AB'' => True
    34	  | .AB'', .BB' => True
    35	  | _, _ => False
    36	
    37	/-- The square-root error obtained by the expanded-observable commutation
    38	argument in `lem:qld-comm-cons`, paper
    39	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:475-505`, blueprint
    40	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:932-1032`. -/
    41	noncomputable def deltaAnticom (ε : ℝ) : ℝ :=
    42	  Real.sqrt ε
    43	
    44	/-- The concrete square-root error is polynomially small in the sense used by
    45	chapters 14 and 15. This discharges the error-function part of
    46	`lem:qld-comm-cons`, blueprint `ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:932-1032`, from the
    47	explicit value proved at paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:503-505`. -/
    48	theorem deltaAnticom_isPolyErr : IsPolyErr deltaAnticom := by
    49	  refine ⟨1, (2 : ℝ)⁻¹, le_rfl, by positivity, ?_⟩
    50	  intro x hx
    51	  constructor
    52	  · exact Real.sqrt_nonneg x
    53	  · rw [deltaAnticom, Real.sqrt_eq_rpow]
    54	    simp
    55	
    56	/-- All expanded-point conclusions at an abstract error function. The first
    57	conjunct lists the four directed cross-party placements; the second lists all
    58	four same-placement commutation conclusions. This proposition collects the
    59	expanded-point conclusions of `lem:qld-comm-cons`, blueprint
    60	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:932-1032`, paper
    61	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:452-505`. -/
    62	def ExpandedPointConclusions (δ : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
    63	  (∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧
    64	    ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ) (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    65	      (p₁ p₂ : Placement), p₁.IsOpposite p₂ →
    66	      ∀ W : PauliKind,
    67	        opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))
    68	          (fun u a => S.place p₁
    69	            ((S.pointMeasExp p₁.side W u).effect a))
    70	          (fun u a => S.place p₂
    71	            ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side W u).effect a))

    24	/--
    25	Squared Euclidean distance between pure states.  Blueprint `def:state-distance`
    26	(`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-179`), paper origin
    27	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.
    28	-/
    29	noncomputable def stateDistSq {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    30	    [DecidableEq ι]
    31	    (ψ φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    32	  ‖ψ - φ‖ ^ 2
    33	
    34	/--
    35	Average squared state-dependent distance between two operator families.  This
    36	is `def:povm-distance` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:203-210`,
    37	with paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.

    39	noncomputable def opFamilyDistSq {X α ι : Type*}
    40	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    41	    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → α → Op ι)
    42	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    43	  avgOver μ (fun x =>
    44	    ∑ a : α, ‖applyOperatorToState (M x a - N x a) ψ‖ ^ 2)
    45

    18	/-- The off-diagonal defect in `def:consistency`, blueprint
    19	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:195-208`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:232-248`. -/
    20	noncomputable def consistencyDefect {X α ι : Type*}
    21	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    22	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    23	    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ι)
    24	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    25	  avgOver μ (fun x =>
    26	    ∑ a : α, ∑ b : α,
    27	      if a = b then 0 else
    28	        (inner ℂ ψ ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ).symm
    29	          ((A x a * B x b).mulVec ψ))).re)
    30	
    31	/-- The quantitative relation in `def:consistency`, blueprint
    32	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:195-208`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:232-248`. -/
    33	def IsConsistentWithin {X α ι : Type*}
    34	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    35	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    36	    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ι)
    37	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (δ : ℝ) : Prop :=
    38	  consistencyDefect μ A B ψ ≤ δ

    41	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:219-226`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`. -/
    42	noncomputable def opDistSq {X ι : Type*}

    44	    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=

  1669	\begin{lemma}
  1670	\label{lem:qld-unitary}
  1671	There exists a function $\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q) = O(\delta_S^{1/4} + md/q)$ (where $\delta_S$ is defined in \Cref{lem:qld-4-7}) and unitaries $V_\alice$ acting on registers $\alice \alice' \alice''$ and $V_\bob$ acting on $\bob \bob' \bob''$ such that 
  1672	\begin{enumerate}
  1673		\item There exists a state $\ket{\aux}$ on registers $\alice \alice' \bob \bob'$ such that
  1674		\[
  1675			\left \| V_\alice \otimes V_\bob \ket{\hat{\psi}}_{\alice \alice' \alice'' \bob \bob' \bob''} - \ket{\aux}_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}_{\alice'' \bob''} \right \|^2 \leq \delta_\qld.
  1676		\]
  1677		
  1678		\item For all $W \in \{X,Z\}, h \in \F_q^\nqubits$
  1679		\begin{align*}
  1680			V_\alice \, \Big(M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \Big)_{\alice} \, V_\alice^\dagger &\approx_{\delta_\qld} \Id_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \\
  1681			 V_\bob \, \Big(M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h  \Big)_{\bob}\, V_\bob^\dagger &\approx_{\delta_\qld} \Id_{\bob \bob'} \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''}
  1682		\end{align*}
  1683		where the $\approx$ statements hold with respect to the state $\ket{\aux}_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}_{\alice'' \bob''}$. 
  1684	\end{enumerate}
  1685	\end{lemma}

  1687	\begin{proof}
  1688	
  1689	Define the linear map
  1690	\[
  1691		V_\alice = \sum_{g_X,g_Z} (\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)))_{\alice ''}\;,
  1692	\]
  1693	where the $\tau^X(\cdot),\tau^Z(\cdot)$ act on $(\C^q)^{\otimes \nqubits}$. (Also note that the argument of $\tau^X$ is $\coded(g_Z)$ and the argument of $\tau^Z$ is $\coded(g_X)$.) We verify the unitarity of $V_\alice$:
  1694	\begin{align*}
  1695		V_\alice V_\alice^\dagger &= \sum_{g_X,g_Z} (\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) )_{\alice ''} \\
  1696		&= \sum_{g_X,g_Z} (\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes \Id_{\alice ''} \\
  1697		&= \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''}
  1698	\end{align*}
  1699	where in the first line we used that the measurement $\{ \hat{S}_{g_\xpt,g_\zpt} \}$  is projective and in the second line we used that the $\tau^Z$ and $\tau^X$ observables are self-inverse. The unitary $V_\bob$ is defined analogously.
  1700	
  1701	Let $\{e_j\}_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}}$ denote the self-dual basis for $\F_q$ over $\F_2$ specified in \Cref{sec:subfields}, and let $\tilde{W}^j$ be the observables introduced in~\eqref{eq:def-tildewj}.   1702	\begin{align*}
  1703		&V_\alice \, \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \, V_\alice^\dagger \\
  1704	  =& \sum_{g_X, g_Z} (-1)^{\tr( e_j(\coded(g_W) \cdot \tilde{u}))} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes \Big ( \tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \\
  1705	  &\hspace{24em}\tau^Z(\coded(g_X))^\dagger \tau^X(\coded(g_Z))^\dagger \Big)_{\alice ''} \\
  1706		 =& \sum_{g_X, g_Z} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes \Big ( \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \Big)_{\alice ''} \\
  1707		 =& \Id_{\alice \alice'} \otimes \Big( \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \Big)_{\alice ''}\;,
  1708	\end{align*}
  1709	where in the third line we used the (anti-)commutation relation
  1710	\[
  1711		\tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) = (-1)^{\tr( e_j(\coded(g_W) \cdot \tilde{u}))} \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \;.
  1712	\]
  1713	An entirely analogous calculation shows that $V_\bob \, \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \, V_\bob^\dagger = \Id_{\bob \bob'} \otimes \Big( \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \Big)_{\bob ''}$.
  1714	
  1715	Next, from the self-consistency property of the observables $\tilde{W}^j$ specified in \Cref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis} we get that for $W \in \{X,Z\}$,
  1716	\[
  1717		\E_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}} \E_{\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits} \bra{\hat{\psi}} \left ( \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \otimes \Id - \Id \otimes \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \right)^\dagger \left ( \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \otimes \Id - \Id \otimes \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \right) \ket{\hat{\psi}} \leq \delta_S\;,
  1718	\]
  1719	which, since $\tilde{W}^j$ is Hermitian, is equivalent to
  1720	\begin{equation}
  1721	\label{eq:qld-unitary-1}
  1722	\E_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}} \E_{\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits} \bra{\hat{\psi}} \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \otimes \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \ket{\hat{\psi}} \geq 1 - \delta_S/2\;.
  1723	\end{equation}
  1724	Let $\ket{\vartheta} = V_\alice \otimes V_\bob \ket{\hat{\psi}}$, and for $W \in \{X,Z\}$ define the operator
  1725	\begin{align*}
  1726		H_W &= \E_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}} \E_{\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits} \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \otimes \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \\
  1727			&= \E_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}} \Big ( \E_{s \in \F_q} \tau^W(e_j s) \otimes \tau^W(e_j s) \Big)^{\otimes \nqubits} \\
  1728			&= \Big ( \E_{s \in \F_q} \tau^W(s) \otimes \tau^W(s) \Big)^{\otimes \nqubits}
  1729	\end{align*}

  1731	\[

  1733	\]
  1734	for $W \in \{X,Z\}$. 
  1735	
  1736	Observe that
  1737	\begin{align*}
  1738		\E_{s,s'} \tau^X(s) \tau^Z(s') \otimes \tau^X(s) \tau^Z(s') &= \E_{s,s'} \sum_{a,b \in \F_q} (-1)^{\tr(as')} \ketbra{a+s}{a} \otimes (-1)^{\tr(bs')} \ketbra{b+s}{b} \\
  1739		&= \E_{s} \sum_{a\in \F_q} \ketbra{a+s}{a} \otimes \ketbra{a+s}{a} \\
  1740		&= \proj{\EPR_q}
  1741	\end{align*}

  1744	\[
  1745		\left \| H_X \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \right\| \leq \left \| \ket{\vartheta} - H_X \ket{\vartheta} \right\| + \left \| \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \right\|\;.

162-  $\sigma_Z$ observables on the tensor product of $n$ EPR pairs. 169-  completeness-soundness gap independent of system size; (iii) a robust protocol for delegated quantum   computation.

    12	\title{The Quoted Quantum Linearity Theorem in the Pauli Basis Analysis}
    13	\author{}
    14	\date{2026-09-03}
    15	
    16	\begin{document}
    17	\maketitle
    18	
    19	\section{At a glance}
    20	
    21	\begin{itemize}
    22	  \item \textbf{Difficulty.} Medium.  The source quotes a fiberwise consequence
    23	  of a state-dependent quantum linearity theorem, but suppresses two averages
    24	  and a compatibility argument for the auxiliary spaces.
    25	  \item \textbf{Estimated weight.} One faithful theorem for a single family,
    26	  followed by a finite common-extension construction that makes the auxiliary space
    27	  uniform over the outer parameters.
    28	  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} Finite direct sums, extensions of
    29	  operators, and squared norms are standard linear algebra.  The imported
    30	  quantum linearity theorem and its state-dependent metric are project-level
    31	  inputs.
    32	  \item \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} Theorem~10 of
    33	  \cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}, finite averaging, and extension by the identity
    34	  on orthogonal summands.  This reduction is tracked in
    35	  \ghissue{19}.
    36	\end{itemize}
    37	
    38	\section{Key theorem forms}
    39	
    40	Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, let $\rho$ be an arbitrary
    41	density operator on $H$, and let $u\mapsto O^u$ be binary observables on $H$,
    42	indexed by $\mathbb F_2^t$.  The cited theorem assumes the averaged
    43	correlation estimate
    44	\[
    45	  \mathop{\mathbb E}_{u,v}
    46	  \operatorname{Tr}\!\left(O^u O^v O^{u+v}\rho\right) \geq 1-\delta.
    47	\]
    48	It produces an auxiliary space $H'$, a unit vector $\mathrm{anc}\in H'$, and
    49	binary observables $L^u$ on $H\otimes H'$ satisfying, with
    50	$\rho'=\rho\otimes|\mathrm{anc}\rangle\langle\mathrm{anc}|$,
    51	\[
    52	  L^uL^v=L^{u+v}
    53	  \quad\text{for every }u,v.
    54	\]
    55	Moreover,
    56	\[
    57	  \mathop{\mathbb E}_{u}
    58	  \operatorname{Tr}\!\left((L^u-O^u\otimes I_{H'})^\dagger
    59	    (L^u-O^u\otimes I_{H'})\,\rho'\right)\leq\delta.
    60	\]
    61	In particular, $L^0=I$: exact linearity gives $(L^0)^2=L^0$, while an
    62	observable is invertible.
    63	
    64	The chapter needs a parameterized version.  For each pair $(x,z)$ it applies
    65	the theorem to $(r,s)\mapsto O^{x,z,r,s}$.  Since the provider theorem accepts
    66	the actual nonnegative defect on each fiber, no assumption that a fiber defect
    67	is at most one, and no good--bad fiber split, is needed.  One must still
    68	formulate the finite common-extension step that makes the auxiliary space
    69	uniform over $(x,z)$.
    70	
    71	\section{Comparison with the quoted statement}
    72	
    73	Lines~711--725 of
    74	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex} quote the
    75	linearity theorem.  The displayed hypothesis correctly averages over both
    76	group variables.  The displayed conclusion, however, says that the corrected
    77	observable is close for every $u$, whereas Theorem~10 of the cited work gives
    78	closeness only on average over $u$ \cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}.  The quotation
    79	also inserts $\delta\leq1$, which is absent from the provider theorem and would
    80	unnecessarily obstruct applying it with a fiber's actual defect.  The assertion
    81	at the identity follows from exact linearity as above.
    82	
    83	Lines~825--832 construct the family $O^{x,z,r,s}$ and establish approximate
    84	linearity only after averaging over $x,z,r,r',s,s'$.  They then apply the
    85	single-family theorem separately for every $(x,z)$ and state that sufficiently
    86	many zero ancillas avoid a further extension.  The remaining implicit step is
    87	to make the theorem's possibly fiber-dependent auxiliary spaces uniform.
    88	
    89	The finite setting admits a standard repair.  Apply the theorem on each fiber
    90	with its actual defect, choose one finite auxiliary space large enough for all
    91	returned spaces, and embed each returned space so that its unit vector maps to
    92	one fixed vector.  Extend the conjugated observables by the identity on the
    93	orthogonal complement.  The embeddings may depend on the fiber because the
    94	observables do.  Averaging then yields the conclusion used later in the
    95	chapter.  This is an open reduction, not a counterexample to the quoted theorem
    96	or to the source's eventual combined-measurement conclusion.
    97	
    98	\section{Blueprint and formalization status}
    99	
   100	Theorem~\path{thm:linearity} and
   101	Remark~\path{rem:linearity-import} in
   102	\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex} record respectively the
   103	averaged provider theorem and the common-ancilla obligation for its fiberwise
   104	use.  The relevant material is at lines~98--147 and 149--191 of that chapter.
   105	
   106	The declaration \path{exists_exactly_linear_observables} in
   107	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean} assumes a nonnegative defect, a
   108	positive semidefinite trace-one operator, binary observables, and the averaged
   109	three-observable correlation.  It returns one finite ancillary space and
   110	normalized ancillary vector for that family, exactly linear binary observables
   111	on the extension, and only the averaged squared-distance bound with the same
   112	defect.  It neither assumes $\delta\leq1$ nor asserts pointwise closeness.  Its
   113	statement therefore matches the provider-faithful blueprint theorem rather
   114	than the strengthened quotation in the QPBT paper.  Its proof remains open,
   115	and no Lean declaration yet supplies the finite common-extension construction
   116	for the family indexed by $(x,z)$.
   117	
   118	Issue~\#19 introduced this discrepancy record for the extraction skeleton;
   119	\ghissue{47} owns the Stage~4.3 proof work consumed downstream.  The chapter-16
   120	extraction declarations consume the concrete \path{GlobalPairWitness}; they
   121	do not assume a new fiberwise linearity hypothesis or a common ancillary space.
   122	
   123	\section{Conclusion}
   124	
   125	The primary discrepancy is a quantifier mismatch in the quotation: the cited
   126	linearity theorem gives average, not pointwise, closeness.  Its use for the
   127	family indexed by $(x,z)$ also requires an explicit finite common-extension
   128	argument.  Both are open formal reductions compatible with the intended
   129	source conclusion.

    12	\title{The Decoding Identity in the Pauli Extraction Argument}
    13	\author{}
    14	\date{2026-09-03}
    15	
    16	\begin{document}
    17	\maketitle
    18	
    19	\section{At a glance}
    20	
    21	\begin{itemize}
    22	  \item \textbf{Difficulty.} Medium.  The source applies a decoder--encoder
    23	  identity to every bounded individual-degree polynomial, although the identity
    24	  is guaranteed for encoded polynomials and can fail outside the encoding image.
    25	  \item \textbf{Estimated weight.} One restricted algebraic identity and one
    26	  probabilistic estimate showing that the constructed measurement assigns
    27	  little state-dependent mass to outcomes outside the encoding image.
    28	  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} Evaluation of the multilinear
    29	  interpolant is elementary polynomial algebra.  The non-encoding-mass bound
    30	  uses project-specific consistency estimates and Schwartz--Zippel.
    31	  \item \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} Multilinear interpolation on the
    32	  Boolean cube, injectivity of the low-degree encoding, measurement
    33	  consistency, and Schwartz--Zippel.  The correction is tracked in
    34	  \ghissue{19}.
    35	\end{itemize}
    36	
    37	\section{Key theorem forms}
    38	
    39	For a word $h\colon\{0,1\}^m\to\mathbb F_q$, let $g_h$ be its multilinear
    40	extension.  Define the chapter's decoder by
    41	\[
    42	  \operatorname{Dec}(g)(y)=g(y),
    43	  \qquad y\in\{0,1\}^m.
    44	\]
    45	Then
    46	\[
    47	  \operatorname{Dec}(g_h)=h
    48	  \quad\text{and}\quad
    49	  \operatorname{Dec}(g_h)\mathbin{\cdot}\operatorname{ind}_m(u)=g_h(u).
    50	\]
    51	More generally, the second identity holds for a polynomial outcome $g$ under
    52	the explicit hypothesis that $g$ belongs to the image of the encoding; no
    53	converse is asserted.
    54	
    55	For an arbitrary bounded individual-degree polynomial $g$, the Boolean values
    56	determine its multilinear interpolant, not necessarily $g$ itself.  The
    57	unrestricted identity
    58	\[
    59	  \operatorname{Dec}(g)\mathbin{\cdot}\operatorname{ind}_m(u)=g(u)
    60	\]
    61	is therefore false.
    62	
    63	\section{Counterexample and source comparison}
    64	
    65	The low-degree encoding is defined at lines~873--897 of
    66	\path{references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex}.  The general decoder at
    67	lines~917--924 retains evaluations lying in a chosen subset $H$; the extraction
    68	chapter instead specifies at lines~1419--1420 of
    69	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex} that the
    70	decoder returns all evaluations on the Boolean cube.  This is the specialization
    71	$H=\mathbb F_q$, rather than the Boolean-valued shorthand used earlier
    72	\cite[lines~873--924 and 1419--1420]{Ji2020MIPStar}.
    73	
    74	Take $m=1$, $d\geq2$, and a field of characteristic two with more than two
    75	elements.  For $g(x)=x^2$, the Boolean evaluations are $g(0)=0$ and $g(1)=1$.
    76	Consequently the decoder is the word whose multilinear extension is $x$.
    77	For any $u\notin\{0,1\}$ with $u^2\neq u$,
    78	\[
    79	  \operatorname{Dec}(g)\mathbin{\cdot}\operatorname{ind}_1(u)=u
    80	  \neq u^2=g(u).
    81	\]
    82	Thus the equality asserted for every $g$ at lines~1483--1492 of the chapter-14
    83	source mirror is false \cite[lines~1483--1492]{Ji2020MIPStar}.  If degrees at
    84	least $q$ are allowed, equality as a function would not by itself prove encoding
    85	membership either, since $x^q$ and $x$ induce the same function on $\mathbb F_q$.
    86	
    87	\section{Required repair}
    88	
    89	The extraction proof must split the marginal measurement into encoding and
    90	non-encoding outcomes.  On encoding outcomes, the restricted identity above
    91	justifies the substitution.  On the complement, the proof must bound
    92	\[
    93	  \sum_{g\ \mathrm{not\ an\ encoding}}
    94	  \langle\widehat\psi,\widehat S_g^W\widehat\psi\rangle.
    95	\]
    96	The blueprint derives an $O(\delta_S)+md/q$ bound from point consistency and
    97	the combined point measurement.  A non-encoding polynomial differs from every
    98	encoded polynomial, so Schwartz--Zippel bounds the probability that their
    99	evaluations coincide.  This estimate is the open reduction; it must be proved
   100	from the paper hypotheses rather than inserted as an extraction hypothesis.
   101	
   102	The printed reindexing at lines~1805--1822 replaces
   103	$g_{\operatorname{Dec}(g_W)}$ by $g_W$, which is the invalid reverse identity
   104	for an arbitrary polynomial outcome.  In the corrected calculation, the
   105	constraint is
   106	$g_h(u)=\operatorname{Dec}(g_W)\mathbin{\cdot}\operatorname{ind}_m(u)-a$.
   107	After setting $h'=h+\operatorname{Dec}(g_W)$, the defining evaluation formula
   108	$g_k(u)=k\mathbin{\cdot}\operatorname{ind}_m(u)$ and characteristic two turn
   109	that constraint into $g_{h'}(u)=a$.  Thus this step uses neither decoder
   110	linearity nor the identity $\operatorname{Dec}(g_h)=h$
   111	\cite[lines~1805--1822]{Ji2020MIPStar}.
   112	
   113	\section{Blueprint and formalization status}
   114	
   115	Definition~\path{def:qld-full-field-decoder} and
   116	Lemmas~\path{lem:qld-decoder-linearity} and
   117	\path{lem:qld-decoder-evaluation} in
   118	\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex} state the full-field
   119	decoder, its linearity and inverse, and the evaluation identity restricted to
   120	encoding outcomes.  Lemma~\path{lem:qld-nonencoding-mass-bound}
   121	separately records the estimate on the remaining outcomes.
   122	
   123	The declarations \path{decodeFq_add}, \path{decodeFq_smul}, and
   124	\path{decodeFq_lowDegreeEncoding} in
   125	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/Decoding.lean} match the three algebraic assertions.
   126	In the same file, \path{IsEncoding} is the equality
   127	$g_{\operatorname{Dec}(g)}=g$ of polynomial representatives, and
   128	\path{decodeFq_dotProduct_indicatorVec} requires an explicit hypothesis
   129	of that predicate.  It therefore matches the corrected evaluation lemma and
   130	does not assert the false unrestricted identity.  Finally,
   131	\path{nonencodingMarginalMass_le} in
   132	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/Consistency.lean} concludes the complementary
   133	mass bound from the projective strategy and global polynomial-pair witness; it
   134	does not add the bound as a witness field or theorem hypothesis.
   135	
   136	These proposition-valued declarations are present with open proofs.  Issue~\#19
   137	owns their Stage~4.2 statements and this discrepancy record; \ghissue{47} owns
   138	the Stage~4.3 decoder calculations and non-encoding support estimate.  No
   139	unrestricted theorem, residual assumption, or additional witness field is
   140	source-faithful.
   141	
   142	\section{Conclusion}
   143	
   144	The decoding identity is false for a general polynomial outcome.  Restricting
   145	it to the encoding image is a necessary local correction.  Recovering the
   146	source's measurement-consistency conclusion then requires the separate
   147	non-encoding-mass estimate, which remains an open proof obligation.

    13	\author{}
    14	\date{2026-09-03}

    16	\begin{document}
    17	\maketitle
    18	
    19	\section{At a glance}
    20	
    21	\begin{itemize}
    22	  \item \textbf{Difficulty.} Medium.  The extraction proof contains two
    23	  incorrect numerical steps and later suppresses the range projection when
    24	  passing from unitary conjugation to isometry conjugation.
    25	  \item \textbf{Estimated weight.} A corrected positive-contraction estimate,
    26	  a small-error case split for normalization, and one range-projection transfer
    27	  lemma for a projective measurement family.
    28	  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} Positivity, contraction inequalities,
    29	  isometry range projections, and norm estimates belong to finite-dimensional
    30	  Hilbert-space algebra.  The state-dependent family distance and register
    31	  placements are project-local.
    32	  \item \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} The inequality
    33	  $H^2\geq2H-I$ for a positive contraction, the triangle inequality, and
    34	  $Q=\phi\phi^\dagger$ for an isometry.  The repair is tracked in
    35	  \ghissue{19}.
    36	\end{itemize}
    37	
    38	\section{Key theorem forms}
    39	
    40	Let $H_X$ and $H_Z$ be the positive contractions of the extraction proof, and
    41	let $\vartheta$ be a unit vector such that
    42	\[
    43	  \langle\vartheta,H_W\vartheta\rangle\geq1-\delta/2
    44	  \qquad (W\in\{X,Z\}).
    45	\]
    46	Since $(I-H_W)^2\geq0$,
    47	\[
    48	  H_W^2\geq2H_W-I,
    49	  \qquad
    50	  \langle\vartheta,H_W^2\vartheta\rangle\geq1-\delta.
    51	\]
    52	Also $\lVert(I-H_W)\vartheta\rVert^2\leq\delta$, whence
    53	\[
    54	  \lVert H_X\vartheta-H_Z\vartheta\rVert^2\leq4\delta.
    55	\]
    56	Together with $H_XH_Z$ equal to the EPR projection, these estimates give the
    57	required overlap bound, with constants absorbed into the stated
    58	$O(\sqrt\delta)$ error.
    59	
    60	For the final transfer, let $\phi\colon\mathcal H\to\mathcal K$ be an isometry
    61	and set $Q=\phi\phi^\dagger$.  If $N_h$ is the unitary-conjugated extension of
    62	a measurement operator $M_h$, then the exact identity is
    63	\[
    64	  \phi M_h\phi^\dagger=N_hQ=QN_h,
    65	\]
    66	not merely $N_h$.  Thus comparison of $N_h$ with an ideal projector must be
    67	combined with control of $(I-Q)\Delta$ on the ideal comparison state
    68	$\Delta$.
    69	
    70	\section{Numerical defects in the source proof}
    71	
    72	Lines~1715--1742 of
    73	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}
    74	construct $H_X,H_Z$ and identify $H_XH_Z$ with the EPR projection.  The norm
    75	estimate at lines~1743--1750 gives
    76	$\lVert(I-H_W)\vartheta\rVert\leq\sqrt\delta$.  At lines~1753--1757 the
    77	source substitutes $\delta$ inside the reverse triangle inequality
    78	\cite[lines~1715--1783]{Ji2020MIPStar}.  That replacement is not valid for
    79	small $\delta$.  The desired lower bound on
    80	$\langle H_W^2\rangle$ follows directly from $H_W^2\geq2H_W-I$, as above.
    81	
    82	The triangle inequality yields
    83	\[
    84	  \lVert H_X\vartheta-H_Z\vartheta\rVert\leq2\sqrt\delta,
    85	\]
    86	so its square is at most $4\delta$.  Line~1761 instead bounds that square by
    87	$2\sqrt\delta$ without a stated restriction.  This inequality follows when
    88	$\delta\leq1/4$; for larger error the theorem is made trivial by enlarging the
    89	universal constant.  The same small-error split ensures that the projected
    90	vector defined at lines~1769--1773 is nonzero before it is normalized.  These
    91	are local numerical repairs and do not weaken the extraction conclusion.
    92	
    93	\section{The range-projection obligation}
    94	
    95	Lines~1827--1858 prove state-dependent closeness for the concrete operators
    96	obtained by conjugating the original measurement with the swap unitaries.
    97	Lines~1864--1875 then define isometries by adjoining EPR pairs and applying
    98	those unitaries, and immediately state the corresponding closeness for
    99	$\phi M_h\phi^\dagger$.  The omitted range projection makes this implication
   100	non-definitional \cite[lines~1827--1875]{Ji2020MIPStar}.
   101	
   102	Let $\Psi$ be the original state and suppose $\phi\Psi$ is close to the ideal
   103	state $\Delta$.  Since $Q\phi\Psi=\phi\Psi$ and $Q$ is a contraction, the
   104	triangle inequality bounds $(I-Q)\Delta$ by the state-extraction error.  Using
   105	$\phi M_h\phi^\dagger=N_hQ$, split
   106	\[
   107	  (N_hQ-T_h)\Delta
   108	  =(N_h-T_h)\Delta-N_h(I-Q)\Delta,
   109	\]
   110	where $T_h$ is the ideal Pauli projector.  Summing squared norms over $h$
   111	uses projectivity and orthogonality to keep the second term under control.
   112	The same argument is required for each player and each Pauli basis.
   113	
   114	This transfer is an open proof obligation for the next extraction stage.  It
   115	must be a theorem derived from the concrete swap unitaries, transformed-state
   116	estimate, and operator comparisons.  It must not be stored as a bridge field,
   117	residual assumption, or hypothesis of the source-labelled soundness theorem.
   118	
   119	\section{Blueprint and formalization status}
   120	
   121	The proof of Lemma~\path{lem:qld-unitary} and the soundness proof in
   122	\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex} use the corrected
   123	positive-contraction estimate, make the small-error case distinction explicit,
   124	and isolate the range-projection calculation.  The chapter therefore preserves
   125	the source's state and observable conclusions while exposing the omitted
   126	argument.
   127	
   128	The structure \path{ExtractionWitness} in
   129	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/Unitary.lean} contains only the two-sided
   130	unitarity equations for the concrete swap maps, a normalized auxiliary state,
   131	the transformed-state estimate, and the two-player Pauli-projector comparison.
   132	The theorem \path{exists_extractionWitness} concludes the existence of this
   133	data at the explicit extraction scale from the projective strategy and its
   134	\path{GlobalPairWitness}; it assumes no range-projection transfer, bridge, or
   135	residual package.  Thus these declarations match the Stage~4.2 extraction
   136	lemma, including the corrected numerical estimates, but do not formalize the
   137	later passage to the isometries in the soundness theorem.  No declaration yet
   138	states that passage.
   139	
   140	Issue~\#19 owns this concrete Stage~4.2 interface and discrepancy record.
   141	\ghissue{47} owns the Stage~4.3 proof of
   142	\path{exists_extractionWitness} and the separate range-projection theorem
   143	needed by \path{pauli_soundness}; that theorem must be derived from the
   144	concrete data rather than stored in the witness.
   145	
   146	\section{Conclusion}
   147	
   148	The printed triangle calculation has repairable numerical errors, and the
   149	last passage from unitaries to isometries omits a genuine range-projection
   150	argument.  Neither defect is a counterexample to Pauli soundness.  The former
   151	is corrected by positive-contraction inequalities and a small-error split;
   152	the latter remains a named downstream proof obligation whose hypotheses are
   153	already supplied by the extraction lemma.

    32	\end{itemize}

    34	\section{Key theorem forms}
    35	
    36	Let $e_0,\ldots,e_{t-1}$ be the fixed self-dual basis of $\mathbb F_q$ over
    37	$\mathbb F_2$.  With the phase convention of the source, generalized Pauli
    38	observables satisfy
    39	\[
    40	  \tau^X(a)\tau^Z(b)
    41	  =(-1)^{\operatorname{tr}(a\mathbin{\cdot}b)}
    42	   \tau^Z(b)\tau^X(a).
    43	\]
    44	Substituting $a=e_j\widetilde u$ and $b=e_{j'}\widetilde v$ gives the exact
    45	relation
    46	\[
    47	  \widetilde X^j(\widetilde u)\widetilde Z^{j'}(\widetilde v)
    48	  =(-1)^{\operatorname{tr}
    49	      (e_je_{j'}(\widetilde u\mathbin{\cdot}\widetilde v))}
    50	   \widetilde Z^{j'}(\widetilde v)\widetilde X^j(\widetilde u).
    51	\]
    52	This formula applies uniformly, whether or not $j=j'$.
    53	
    54	\section{The false dichotomy in the source}
    55	
    56	Lines~1438--1450 of
    57	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}
    58	identify each extracted observable with a tensor product containing
    59	$\tau^W(e_j\widetilde u)$.  Lines~1451--1456 then claim that the extracted
    60	$X$- and $Z$-observables commute whenever $j\neq j'$
    61	\cite[lines~1438--1456]{Ji2020MIPStar}.  Self-duality gives only
    62	\[
    63	  \operatorname{tr}(e_je_{j'})=0 \qquad (j\neq j').
    64	\]
    65	It does not imply
    66	\[
    67	  \operatorname{tr}(e_je_{j'}s)=0
    68	  \qquad\text{for every }s\in\mathbb F_q.
    69	\]
    70	
    71	Indeed, for distinct $j,j'$, the element $c=e_je_{j'}$ is nonzero.  The trace
    72	pairing is nondegenerate, so there is an $s\in\mathbb F_q$ for which
    73	$\operatorname{tr}(cs)=1$.  Taking vectors whose first coordinates are $1$
    74	and $s$, with all remaining coordinates zero, gives
    75	$\widetilde u\mathbin{\cdot}\widetilde v=s$.  The two extracted observables
    76	then anticommute.  This is a counterexample to the printed cross-basis
    77	commutation assertion.
    78	
    79	When $\widetilde u\mathbin{\cdot}\widetilde v$ lies in the prime field, the
    80	printed distinction is recovered from self-duality.  The chapter quantifies
    81	over arbitrary vectors, however, so that special case does not repair its
    82	statement.

    85

    92	$j,j'$ over the zero-based type

    95	\textbf{Local fix} marker.  Thus the Lean statement agrees with the corrected
    96	blueprint and deliberately differs from the false cross-basis commutation
    97	claim in the paper; it introduces no extra hypothesis.
    98

   100	Stage~4.2 statement and this discrepancy record; \ghissue{47} owns the
   101	Stage~4.3 proof from the product form and generalized Pauli commutation.
   102	
   103	This correction changes neither the definition of the extracted observables
   104	nor the source-faithful consistency and extraction conclusions.  It repairs an
   105	auxiliary algebraic assertion that is independent of the robustness estimates.
   106	
   107	\section{Conclusion}
   108	
   109	The source's cross-basis commutation claim is false for general
   110	$\widetilde u$ and $\widetilde v$.  The correct relation retains the phase
   111	$(-1)^{\operatorname{tr}(e_je_{j'}(\widetilde u\cdot\widetilde v))}$.
   112	Because the later argument does not invoke the false dichotomy, this is a
   113	local correction rather than an additional hypothesis on the extraction
   114	theorem.

Neither the linearity test nor the
anticommutation test \emph{alone} would be  sufficient to achieve the
conclusion: as noted above, the linearity test can be passed even by
classical provers, and our anticommutation test can be fooled if the
provers share just one EPR pair. Rather, it is the guarantees provided
by these tests together that enable us to create a tensor-product
structure in the provers' Hilbert space. 

To gain intuition on the test one may think of it in the following way. A standard approach to self-testing $n$ EPR pairs is to fix a decomposition of the Hilbert space as 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c2n}
\mH = \C^{2^n} \approx \C^2 \otimes \cdots \otimes \C^2,
\end{equation}
and perform the CHSH (or Magic Square) test ``in parallel'', on each copy of $\C^2$. To the best of our knowledge such test only leads to robustness bounds with a polynomial dependence in $n$. In contrast the test on which Theorem~\ref{thm:braiding} is based relies on the observation that the decomposition~\eqref{eq:c2n} need not be rigidly fixed a priori; indeed there are many bases in which such decomposition of $\C^{2^n}$ in tensor factors can be performed. In particular,  \emph{any} pair of anti-commuting observables on $\mH$ suffices to specify a copy of $\C^2$, on which a CHSH test can in principle be performed (here we crucially rely on rotation invariance of the $2^n$-dimensional maximally entangled state). Our test leverages this observation by performing a CHSH test for each possible pair of Pauli operators ($\sigma_X(a)$, $\sigma_Z(b)$), where $a,b\in\{0,1\}^n$ are such that $a\cdot b=1$. Each of these tests amounts to identifying a copy of $\C^2$ and performing the CHSH test on it. Contrary to the parallel-repeated CHSH test these copies are not independent, and this is what makes our test much more robust. 

\paragraph{Encoding quantum states.}
The second component of the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:main_informal} is a
procedure, first introduced in~\cite{FV14,ji2015classical}, for
encoding an $n$-qubit quantum state in a constant number of $n$-qubit
shares such that certain properties of the encoded state (such as
expectation values of local Pauli observables) can be verified through
a classical interaction with provers each holding one of the
shares. This is akin to how the ``games'' variant of the classical PCP
theorem is derived from the ``proof-checking'' variant: while in the
classical setting a proof can be directly shared across multiple
provers, in the quantum setting we use a form of secret-sharing code
that allows for distributing quantum information.

This procedure is efficient in that the total number of tests that can
be performed (equivalently, the number of questions) is polynomial in
$n$. However, the test in~\cite{FV14,ji2015classical} is not robust,
and is only able to provide meaningful results for values of $\eps$
that scale inverse-polynomially with $n$. By extending the Pauli
braiding test, Theorem~\ref{thm:braiding}, to the stabilizer framework
of~\cite{ji2015classical} we obtain a procedure which is meaningful
for constant $\eps$. The drawback is that the provers may now be asked
to measure all their qubits, and questions have length linear in $n$;
however the total effort required of the classical verifier (and of provers given access to the state) remains
polynomial in the size of the instance.






\subsection{Related work}
\label{sec:related}

We build on a number of previous works in quantum information
and complexity theory. 
Motivation for the problem we consider goes back to a question of Aharonov and Ben-Or (personal communication, 2013), who asked how a quantum generalization of the exponential classical PCP could look like if it was not derived through the ``circuitous route'' obtained as the compilation of known but complex results from the theory of classical and quantum interactive proof systems (as described earlier). In this respect we point to~\cite[Section
  5]{AharonovAV13qpcp} for a very different approach to the same question based on a ``quantum take'' on the arithmetization technique. 
	
  More directly, our work builds on the already-mentioned
  works~\cite{FV14, ji2015classical} initiating the study of
  entangled-prover interactive proof systems for the local Hamiltonian
  problem. The idea of using a distributed encoding of the ground
  state in order to obtain a multiprover interactive proof system for
  the ground state energy is introduced in~\cite{FV14}. In that work
  the protocol required the provers to return qubits; the possibility
  for making the protocol purely classical was uncovered by
  Ji~\cite{ji2015classical}. Our use of stabilizer codes, and the
  stabilizer test which forms part of our protocol, originate in his
  work. In addition we borrow from ideas introduced in the study of 
quantum multiprover interactive proofs with entangled provers~\cite{KM03, CHTW04}, and especially the three-prover linearity test of~\cite{IV12} and the use of oracularization from~\cite{IKM09} to make it into a two-prover test.

Our results are related to work in quantum self-testing, in particular testing EPR
pairs~\cite{McKagueYS12rigidity} and more general entangled
states~\cite{mckague2014self}. A sequence of results has established that the presence of $n$ EPR pairs between two provers can be certified via a protocol
using queries and answers of length polynomial in $n$, with
inverse-polynomial completeness-soundness gap. This was first
achieved by~\cite{ReichardtUV13nature} for a test based on serial
repetition of the CHSH game, and subsequently by~\cite{McKague15} for
a single-round test based on CHSH, by~\cite{OV16} for an XOR game
based on CHSH, and by~\cite{CN16}
and~\cite{Coladangelo16} independently for the parallel-repeated Magic
Square game. Viewed in the context of these results our work is the only one to provide a test whose robustness does not depend on the number of EPR pairs being tested. The reason this can be achieved is the linearity test(s) performed as part of the Pauli braiding test, which we see as a major innovation of our work.

  1618		\begin{gather}
  1619			\label{eq:qld-sg-cons2}
  1620			(\hat{S}^W_g \cdot (\Id - \hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{g(u)}))_{\alice \alice'} \approx_{\delta_S} 0
  1621		\end{gather}
  1622		where the answer summation is over $g \in \ideg_{d,m}(\F_q)$.
  1623	      Furthermore, all symmetric equivalents of these approximations
  1624	      also hold.
  1625	\end{lemma}
  1626	\begin{proof}
  1627	We first prove \Cref{eq:qld-sg-cons}. From \Cref{eq:qld-s-point-con-alice} of \Cref{lem:qld-4-7} we have that on average over $u \in \F_q^m$,
  1628	\begin{equation}
  1629	\label{eq:qld-constructing-the-paulis-helper0}
  1630		  \bra{\hat{\psi}} \sum_g (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{g(u)})_{\bob \alice''} \ket{\hat{\psi}} \geq 1 - \delta_S
  1631	\end{equation}
  1632	which is equivalent to $\sum_g (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{g(u)})_{\bob \alice''}  \simeq_{\delta_S} \Id$. By \Cref{fact:agreement}, we have that
  1633	\[
  1634	\sum_g (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{g(u)})_{\bob \alice''} \approx_{\delta_S} \Id.
  1635	\]
  1636

  1638	\[ (\hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]})_{\alice \alice'} \approx_{\delta_S} (\hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{a})_{\bob \alice''}\]
  1639	where the answer summation is over $a \in \F_q$. Left-multiplying this expression by $(\hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]})_{\alice \alice'}$ and using \Cref{fact:add-a-proj} we get
  1640	\begin{align*}
  1641	(\hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]})_{\alice \alice'} &\approx_{\delta_S} (\hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{a})_{\bob \alice''} \\
  1642	&\approx_\eps (\hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]} \cdot \hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{a})_{\alice \alice'}
  1643	\end{align*}
  1644	where the second approximation follows from the following calculation:
  1645	\begin{align}
  1646		& \E_u \sum_a \left \| (\hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]})_{\alice \alice'} \cdot \Big ( (\hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{a})_{\alice \alice'} - (\hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{a})_{\bob \alice''} \Big ) \ket{\hat{\psi}} \right \|^2  \\
  1647		\leq & \E_u \sum_a \bra{\hat{\psi}} \Big ( (\hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{a})_{\alice \alice'} - (\hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{a})_{\bob \alice''} \Big )^2 \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
  1648		= & \E_u \sum_a \left \| (\hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{a})_{\alice \alice'} - (\hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{a})_{\bob \alice''} \ket{\hat{\psi}} \right \|^2 \\
  1649		\leq & \eps
  1650	\end{align}
  1651	The first inequality follows from the fact that $\hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]} \leq \Id$ for all $a$, and the second inequality follows from the self-consistency of $\hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{a}$ (established in \Cref{lem:qld-comm-cons}). Thus
  1652	\[
  1653		(\hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]})_{\alice \alice'} \approx_{O(\delta_S + \eps)} (\hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]} \cdot \hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{a})_{\alice \alice'}~.
  1654	\]
  1655	On the other hand, notice that
  1656	\begin{align*}
  1657		&\E_u \sum_g \left \| (\hat{S}^W_{g} \cdot (\Id - \hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{g(u)}))_{\alice \alice'} \ket{\hat{\psi}} \right \|^2 \\
  1658		=& \E_u \sum_g \bra{\hat{\psi}} ((\Id - \hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{g(u)}) \cdot \hat{S}^W_{g} \cdot (\Id - \hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{g(u)}))_{\alice \alice'} \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
  1659		=& \E_u \sum_a \bra{\hat{\psi}} ((\Id - \hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{a}) \cdot \hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]} \cdot (\Id - \hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{a}))_{\alice \alice'} \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
  1660		\leq& O(\delta_S + \eps).
  1661	\end{align*}
  1662	\Cref{eq:qld-sg-cons2} is thus obtained by absorbing $\eps$ into the function $\delta_S$.  
  1663	\end{proof}

     3	/-!
     4	# The low-degree encoding
     5	
     6	This module encodes the Boolean subcube by multilinear indicator polynomials
     7	and packages the resulting low-degree code as honest polynomial representatives.
     8	
     9	## References
    10	
    11	The source-facing nodes are `def:polynomials-degree`,
    12	`def:low-degree-encoding`, and `def:indicator-vector` in
    13	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:321-417`; the paper origin is
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    15	The polynomial class `def:polyfunc` is reused from
    16	`MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc` (the LDT formalization).
    17	-/
    18	
    19	open scoped BigOperators
    20	open MvPolynomial
    21	
    22	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    23	
    24	/- The Boolean cube indexes the `2^m` qudits in the low-degree encoding. -/
    25	/-- The Boolean cube indexing the `2^m` qudits of the test.  This is the index
    26	type in `def:low-degree-encoding`, blueprint
    27	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:381-401`, paper origin
    28	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    29	-/
    30	abbrev Cube (m : ℕ) := Fin m → Bool
    31	
    32	/--
    33	The representative polynomial which is `1` at `y` on the Boolean cube and
    34	zero at the other cube points.  This is the indicator polynomial in
    35	`def:low-degree-encoding` (blueprint lines 381-401; paper
    36	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`).
    37	-/
    38	noncomputable def indicatorPoly {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ} (y : Cube m) :
    39	    MvPolynomial (Fin m) K :=
    40	  ∏ i : Fin m, if y i then X i else (1 - X i)
    41	
    42	/--
    43	The multilinear low-degree encoding of a coefficient string.  Polynomial
    44	representatives are used, as fixed by issue #0004, rather than quotienting by
    45	functional equality.  Blueprint: `def:low-degree-encoding`,
    46	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:381-401`; paper origin:
    47	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    48	-/
    49	noncomputable def lowDegreeEncoding {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    50	    (a : Cube m → K) : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K :=
    51	  ∑ y : Cube m, a y • indicatorPoly y
    52	
    53	/- Evaluation shorthand for the representative polynomial in
    54	`def:low-degree-encoding`; it is Lean-only notation. -/
    55	/-- Evaluation shorthand for the low-degree encoding.  Blueprint
    56	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:381-401`, paper origin
    57	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    58	-/
    59	noncomputable def lowDegreeEnc {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    60	    (a : Cube m → K) (x : Fin m → K) : K :=
    61	  eval x (lowDegreeEncoding a)
    62	
    63	/--
    64	The indicator vector `ind_m(x)` of `def:indicator-vector`.
    65	Blueprint: `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:403-417`; paper origin:
    66	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    67	-/
    68	noncomputable def indicatorVec {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    69	    (x : Fin m → K) : Cube m → K :=
    70	  fun y => eval x (indicatorPoly y)
    71	
    72	/--
    73	The defining dot-product identity for the encoding, corresponding to
    74	Equation `eq:low-degree-encoding-definition` and `def:indicator-vector` in the
    75	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:403-417`, paper origin
    76	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    77	-/
    78	theorem lowDegreeEnc_eq_dotProduct {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    79	    (a : Cube m → K) (x : Fin m → K) :
    80	    lowDegreeEnc a x = dotProduct a (indicatorVec x) := by
    81	  simp [lowDegreeEnc, lowDegreeEncoding, indicatorVec, dotProduct]
    82	
    83	end MIPStarRE.QPBT
